Continue building Trueup in this repository. Read README.md, hackathon.md, CHANGELOG.md and src/ first. This session is recorded by Entire and published: work only inside this repository and never mention anything outside it. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it (no background commands; long timeouts). Do not git commit or push. Never print or write the values of TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY or any key. Memory is limited: one library at a time. Model: claude-sonnet-4.6 only, the $15 spending guard stays on.

Task: the fixer and the verifier, then fix the two headline findings for real.
1. Locate (`src/trueup/fixer/locate.py`): use Entire's code graph on a shallow clone of the library under `.trueup/clones/<lib>` to find the wrapper function and its callers. Run `entire agent-help` and `entire agent-help labs` (and any graph/search subcommand it lists) to learn the exact, currently installed commands; do not guess flags. Save the graph output per finding in the run directory. If the graph isn't available for this repo or plan, fall back to ripgrep plus Python's ast, and record honestly that the graph was not used and why.
2. Patch (`src/trueup/fixer/patch.py`): the model drafts the smallest change, modelled on the library that gets it right or the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, plus a unit test in the library's own test style that fails before and passes after. The model proposes; code applies the patch to the clone and decides.
3. Verify (`src/trueup/fixer/verify.py`): (a) the library's own test suite for that package passes, or shows the same failures as before the patch, listed; (b) the scenario that found it now matches truth; (c) the full scenario library shows no new mismatches for that library (install the patched package into a separate venv); (d) a before/after table is stored. If the patch breaks the library's tests, the fixer revises it, at most 3 tries, then the finding ships without a fix and says so. Every try is recorded (this is the "action failed, what the agent did next" evidence).
4. CLI: `trueup fix <finding-id>` writes `fixes/<finding-id>/` with patch.diff, test file, before/after table, suite results, graph output and the try log. Traced in neatlogs as workflows `trueup-fixer` and `trueup-verifier`.
5. Run it for real on: (a) OpenLLMetry, OpenAI Agents SDK non-streamed runs record two LLM spans per call (double calls and tokens); (b) OpenInference, a crashed Agents SDK run shows OK at the top-level span. If time and budget allow, also (c) neatlogs, the new finding that a failed `messages.stream()` shows OK. Record in hackathon.md: each try, why it failed or passed, suite results, before/after numbers, and model cost (from the key's spend). Do not call anything "fixed" without a passing test and the scenario now matching truth.
6. `trueup upstream <finding-id>`: draft issue text and PR text into `upstream/<finding-id>/` (symptom, boundary, minimal standalone repro under 40 lines that needs only the library and the SDK, before/after table, environment), following the repo's issue template if it has one. Never post anything.

Update CHANGELOG.md and README status. Plain words, no filler. `uv run pytest -q` must pass. Finish with a summary.
I'll start by reading the project docs and source.

input.command: cat README.md hackathon.md CHANGELOG.md | head -400 && find src tests -name '*.py' | head -80 && ls -a

result.output:
Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

`trueup doctor`, `trueup sweep <neatlogs|openinference|openllmetry>`, `trueup audit <script> --library <lib>`, `trueup check <run_id|latest> --library <lib>` and `trueup plan <lib> [--max N]` work.

`sweep` runs the scenarios (plain SDK, LangChain/LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK; pick with `--framework`) against a fake provider, compares truth with the trace, prints a table of leads and writes truth, trace and `leads.json` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace; it is not a confirmed bug.

`audit` runs your script's `main()` against the fake (through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) under the chosen library, once per fake scenario on each provider route the script calls, and compares the same way. It needs a `main()` with no arguments that uses the `openai` or `anthropic` SDK; see `src/trueup/audit.py` for its limits.

`check` runs the checker over a sweep's leads. A lead becomes a finding only if it reproduces twice in fresh processes, on the recommended setup, on the latest release and on the library's main branch, the fake really sent what truth says, the harness is sane, another library or the OpenTelemetry conventions show the right behaviour, and a repro under 40 lines shows it. Otherwise it is withdrawn with the rule that failed (kept and counted). Findings that share a cause are grouped, then searched for in the library's GitHub issues and PRs (read only). It writes `findings.json` and `withdrawn.json` in the run dir.

`plan` asks a model (`claude-sonnet-4.6` through an OpenAI-compatible proxy) for new scenarios, given the library's wrapper source, the scenario library and the latest findings. A proposal is JSON data: an existing app plus an existing fake behaviour, with the truth it expects. Code checks the schema, that the app and fake behaviour exist and fit, that the pair is new, and runs the app untraced to confirm the truth. A rejected proposal goes back to the model with the reason, twice at most. Accepted ones are saved to `scenarios/proposed/<lib>/`; `trueup sweep <lib> --proposed [FROM]` runs them. Before every model call Trueup reads the key's spend from the proxy and stops at $15. It needs `TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY` and `TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL`.

Commands that call the model trace Trueup itself to neatlogs when `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set: one session per run (session id = run id), one trace per worker. The scenario runs stay local: their subprocesses get no neatlogs key and have export turned off.

`doctor` also makes one GET each to neatlogs and the model proxy (no model call).

The other commands (`fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no leads, 1 leads found, 2 could not run.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
uv sync
uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q         # offline unit tests
uv run pytest -q -m e2e  # builds per-library venvs, runs subprocesses
uv run trueup sweep neatlogs
uv run trueup sweep openllmetry --framework openai-agents
uv run trueup audit examples/agent.py --library openinference
uv run trueup check latest --library neatlogs
uv run trueup plan openllmetry --max 3
uv run trueup sweep openllmetry --proposed
```

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
# Build log

neatHack, 10-12 Oct 2026.

## 2026-10-10: skeleton

- Set up the uv project (Python 3.12, src layout) with the `trueup` command.
- Added the data model in `trueup.core`: Observation, Mismatch, Run, Finding and Severity, each with `to_dict`/`from_dict`.
- `trueup doctor` reports the Python version and whether the two keys are set, without printing them. Other commands exit 2 with "not built yet".
- Tests for the round trip, severity order and doctor. CI runs them on push.
- Nothing is audited yet. No findings so far.

## 2026-10-10: the truth side

- `trueup.fake`: a local fake provider (stdlib http.server in a thread, random free port). It speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. The request's model name picks the scenario: plain, streamed with and without usage, two parallel tool calls with split streamed arguments, refusal, n=2, HTTP 500 and 529, error event mid-stream, status failed and incomplete, reasoning summary, thinking, tool_use with input_json_delta, and a dropped connection. Every id is unique per call and per fake instance. The truth log records each request and what was sent back, including tokens per call, or that no usage was sent.
- 34 fixture tests run the real `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs against the fake. Two SDK behaviours we found and recorded: the openai SDK passes a Responses `error` event to the app instead of raising, and the anthropic SDK lets a dropped stream through as a raw `RemoteProtocolError`, not an SDK exception.
- `trueup.scenarios`: 31 plain-SDK scenarios as data (chat 12, Responses 9, Anthropic 10), each with expected truth. A unit test runs every app with no tracing library and checks the expectations against what really happens. That check caught one wrong expectation (streamed tool calls without include_usage carry no tokens). 20 LangChain/LangGraph/OpenAI Agents cases are listed as not_built.
- `trueup.runner`: runs one scenario in a fresh subprocess in `.trueup/venvs/<lib>` (built with uv), using the library's recommended setup and an in-memory span exporter. It returns truth plus spans as JSON. A scenario that cannot run is reported NOT RUN with the reason.
- Regression tests for four traps: reused response ids, a reused async client across asyncio.run, a missing-usage reply read as a bug, and neatlogs exporting to a dead endpoint.
- `trueup sweep <library>` writes observations and `summary.txt` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. All three libraries ran 31/31. The first openllmetry sweep was 0/31 NOT RUN because `traceloop-sdk` imports `httpx` without declaring it; we now install `httpx` in that venv.
- Leads for the comparer (not judged yet): neatlogs adds `stream_options.include_usage` to the app's streamed chat request. openinference exports no span for a stream closed early, or for a Responses stream that ends with an error event. openllmetry marks chat streams that raised (error event, cut) as OK, and exports no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream errors and cuts.

## 2026-10-10: the comparer and the reports

- `trueup.core.compare` checks truth against the spans: run status, call status, call count, span closed, tokens, output (text, refusal, tool calls with arguments compared as JSON), finish, plus a "request changed" note. Severity: HIGH changes a number or status a dashboard shows by default, MEDIUM is wrong or missing span detail, LOW is extra or cosmetic.
- `trueup.core.adapters`: one data-driven adapter per library saying where it keeps tokens, finish reasons, outputs and response ids. Tested against span JSON from the sweeps, saved in `tests/fixtures/spans/` with stack traces and local URLs removed. OpenLLMetry error spans for failed Responses streams have no `gen_ai.operation.name`, so its adapter keys on `gen_ai.provider.name`.
- Choices made while comparing: finish reasons are compared through a synonym table (end_turn = stop, tool_use = tool_calls = tool_call, incomplete = length), because OpenLLMetry normalises them; a completed Responses call that asked for a tool may show `tool_call`. When the app closes a stream early, output, tokens and finish are not compared, since the app never got them. Tokens are only compared when the fake sent usage. Spans are matched to calls by response id, then by start order.
- A mismatch is called a lead. `trueup sweep <lib>` now prints a leads table, writes `leads.json` and exits 1 if there is any lead.
- `trueup audit <agent.py> --library <lib>` runs the script's `main()` against the fake, once per fake scenario on each route the script calls, and compares. Limits are written in `src/trueup/audit.py`. Tried on `examples/agent.py` under openinference: 8 runs, 1 lead (refusal not recorded).

Sweeps after the comparer (31/31 ran for each library). These are leads, not confirmed bugs; the self-check comes next.

| library | leads | high | medium | low | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 22 | 4 | 18 | 0 | 5 |
| openinference | 10 | 2 | 8 | 0 | 0 |
| openllmetry | 14 | 11 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

Leads per check:

| check | neatlogs | openinference | openllmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_status | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| call_status | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| call_count | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| span_closed | 0 | 2 | 4 |
| tokens | 3 | 0 | 4 |
| output | 7 | 1 | 0 |
| finish | 10 | 7 | 0 |

- neatlogs: Anthropic `messages.stream` spans carry no tokens, text, tool calls or finish reason (3 scenarios); Responses spans carry no status/finish (7) and no function calls (2); the chat refusal is not recorded; the Responses stream that ends with an error event stays UNSET with no exception event. The 5 notes are neatlogs adding `stream_options.include_usage` to streamed chat requests; tokens were compared against what the fake really sent.
- openinference: no span for a chat stream closed early or for a Responses stream ending in an error event; Responses spans carry no status/finish (7); the chat refusal is not recorded.
- openllmetry: chat streams that raised (error event, cut) and the Responses error-event stream end OK; no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream error/cut; Anthropic streamed spans record 4 output tokens where the provider sent 3 (4 scenarios).

## 2026-10-10: framework scenarios

- The fake now runs agent flows. It picks each reply from the request, so it keeps no state: no tool result yet means a tool call, a tool result means the answer. Chat Completions: one tool, two parallel tools, a loop that always asks for the tool, and HTTP 500 on the second call. Responses (for the OpenAI Agents SDK): one tool, a loop, 500 on the second call, a tool name the agent does not have, and an error event or a dropped connection in the streamed answer, after the full streamed event sequence of the first call. Fixture tests run them through the real openai SDK, LangChain, LangGraph and the Agents SDK.
- 20 framework scenarios are built: LangChain 6, LangGraph 6, OpenAI Agents SDK 8. Each has expected truth, including which tools really ran and which raised. The untraced check runs all 51 scenarios with the real SDKs. Two things it showed: LangGraph's `create_react_agent` does not raise at the step limit (it answers "Sorry, need more steps"), and langchain-openai raises its own `OpenAIAPIError` and `OpenAIConnectionError`.
- Setups per framework. neatlogs: `neatlogs.init(instrumentations=[...])` with its README keys (`langchain`, `langchain`+`langgraph`, `openai_agents`), export off. OpenInference: `LangChainInstrumentor` or `OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor`, and the OpenAI/Anthropic ones only for plain SDK runs. OpenLLMetry: `Traceloop.init(exporter=<in-memory>, disable_batch=True)` for everything. The Agents SDK's own uploader to api.openai.com is removed; the instrumentors' processors stay. Each agent gets its own AsyncOpenAI client.
- Trap found: the first neatlogs LangChain run exported no spans and raised no error. neatlogs checks `import langchain`, and the venv had `langchain-core` and `langchain-openai` but not `langchain`, so it logged "Skipped: langchain (not installed)". Every venv now installs `langchain`. Before a framework scenario runs, the runner checks that the framework imports and that an instrumentor for it is active, and reports NOT RUN with the reason if not. A regression test covers this.
- Comparer: run status uses the trace root (for the Agents SDK, "Agent workflow"). Two new checks. `tools`: every tool that really ran has a tool span, and a tool that raised has an ERROR span or an exception event. `error_recorded`: when the app raised but no provider call failed (unknown tool, max turns), some span must record an error. The OpenLLMetry adapter no longer counts LangGraph task, tool, agent and workflow spans as LLM calls. A scenario can say the app itself asked for stream usage, so LangChain's `stream_usage=True` is not reported as the library changing the request.

Sweeps with all 51 scenarios (runs `20261010T203332Z-neatlogs`, `20261010T203600Z-openinference`, `20261010T203755Z-openllmetry`). 51/51 ran for each library; nothing NOT RUN. The plain-SDK counts are unchanged from the last sweep. These are leads, not confirmed bugs.

| library | leads | high | medium | low | notes | of which framework |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 58 | 9 | 49 | 0 | 5 | 36 (high 5, medium 31) |
| openinference | 19 | 7 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 9 (high 5, medium 4) |
| openllmetry | 29 | 21 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 15 (high 10, medium 5) |

Leads per check (all scenarios; framework scenarios in brackets):

| check | neatlogs | openinference | openllmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_status | 6 (5) | 5 (5) | 8 (5) |
| call_status | 4 (3) | 3 (3) | 6 (3) |
| call_count | 0 | 0 | 5 (5) |
| span_closed | 0 | 2 (0) | 4 (0) |
| tokens | 3 (0) | 0 | 4 (0) |
| output | 8 (1) | 2 (1) | 1 (1) |
| finish | 37 (27) | 7 (0) | 0 |
| tools | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| error_recorded | 0 | 0 | 1 (1) |

- All three: when an Agents SDK run raises (500 on the second call, max turns, unknown tool, streamed error event, streamed cut), the root "Agent workflow" span is OK (5 scenarios each). For the provider failures the inner `response` span is ERROR but has no exception event (3 each). The LangChain refusal is not recorded as output (1 each). Tool spans were right everywhere, including the raised tool.
- neatlogs: framework LLM spans have no `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` (27). The OpenInference `llm.finish_reason` is on the same span; the adapter reads the neatlogs namespace only, as in the plain-SDK sweeps.
- openllmetry: in non-streamed Agents SDK runs every model call gets two LLM spans, one from the Agents SDK instrumentation and one from the OpenAI instrumentation under it. That doubles calls and tokens (ag-run: 2 calls and 36 tokens really; 4 spans and 72 tokens in the trace). Streamed runs get one span per call. The unknown-tool error is on no span: `no_such_tool` only appears as the tool call in the model's output.

Answers to the three questions:
1. Does a crashed Agents SDK run show OK at the top level? Yes, in all three libraries, in all 5 crash scenarios.
2. Does OpenLLMetry with Traceloop.init double LLM calls and tokens for the Agents SDK? Yes in non-streamed runs (5 of 5 scenarios, exactly 2x). Streamed runs are not affected (3 of 3 have one span per call and the right tokens).
3. Does an unknown-tool error appear anywhere in the trace? neatlogs and OpenInference: only as the status description of the `turn` span (ERROR, no exception event); the root stays OK. OpenLLMetry: nowhere.

## 2026-10-10: the checker and the deduper

- `trueup check <run_id|latest> --library <lib>` takes a sweep's leads through seven rules: reproduces twice in fresh processes; recommended setup with the framework installed; latest release (checked against PyPI) and the library's main branch (shallow clone, installed into `.trueup/venvs/<lib>-main`); the fake sent what truth claims; harness sane (own client per event loop, export off, no endpoint); another library or the OTel conventions show the right behaviour; a repro under 40 lines reproduces it. A lead that passes every rule is a finding; otherwise it is withdrawn with the failing rule, kept as a lead, or marked "disputed semantics". Withdrawn leads stay in `withdrawn.json`.
- Findings with the same library, check, field and code path are grouped into one finding with a list of scenarios.
- The deduper searches each library's issues and PRs (all states, `gh search issues --include-prs`), lists the integration's titles and records each search with its date (in `findings.json`). Read only: nothing was opened, commented on or posted.
- Repros are generated per scenario in `.trueup/runs/<run>/repros/` (31 lines each). They run offline with fake keys, but they import trueup for the fake provider and the app code, so they are not yet standalone scripts for an upstream issue.

### Trueup's own false alarm: neatlogs finish reason

The neatlogs adapter read the finish reason only from `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` / `neatlogs.llm.choices.N.finish_reason`. In the real spans from run `20261010T203332Z-neatlogs`, every framework LLM span (LangChain, LangGraph, Agents SDK) comes from an OpenInference instrumentor (scope `openinference.instrumentation.langchain` / `.openai_agents`). These spans carry the right finish reason in `llm.finish_reason`. neatlogs copies tokens and tool calls into its own namespace but not the finish reason. The finish reason is in the exported trace, so the leads were ours. The adapter now also reads `llm.finish_reason`.

Same saved run, compared again: 58 leads before, 31 after. All 27 removed leads were `finish` leads on framework scenarios: ag-bad-tool 1, ag-llm-fails 1, ag-max-turns 3, ag-run 2, ag-streamed 2, ag-streamed-cut 1, ag-streamed-error 1, ag-tool-raises 2, lc-invoke 1, lc-refusal 1, lc-stream 1, lg-agent 2, lg-llm-fails 1, lg-parallel 2, lg-step-limit 3, lg-stream 2, lg-tool-raises 1. The 10 plain-SDK finish leads stay. Whether the neatlogs dashboard shows `llm.finish_reason` was not checked.

### Results

Checked against the latest releases (neatlogs 1.4.26; OpenInference openai 0.1.65, anthropic 3.0.3, langchain 0.1.79, openai-agents 2.5.3; OpenLLMetry 0.62.4, all equal to PyPI) and main (neatlogs `202f8776ea`, openinference `c364180e5b`, openllmetry `df4921a409`). Every main branch installed.

| library | leads | finding leads | findings (grouped) | high | medium | withdrawn | disputed | already known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 31 | 27 | 12 | 3 | 9 | 0 | 2 groups (4 leads) | 3 |
| openinference | 19 | 15 | 6 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 2 groups (4 leads) | 0 |
| openllmetry | 29 | 23 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 2 (latest_and_main) | 2 groups (4 leads) | 1 |

Withdrawn: openllmetry, oa-resp-failed and oa-resp-incomplete (no span for a Responses call with status failed or incomplete). Both reproduce on 0.62.4 but not on main, so they are fixed there.

Disputed semantics, in all three libraries: (1) on Agents SDK provider failures the `response` span is ERROR but has no exception event (ag-llm-fails, ag-streamed-error, ag-streamed-cut); the conventions require the status, not the event. (2) the LangChain refusal is not recorded as output (lc-refusal); the GenAI conventions have no refusal part and no library records it.

neatlogs findings:
- HIGH: Agents SDK run that raises (5 scenarios): root "Agent workflow" span is OK.
- HIGH: Responses stream ending in an error event: top-level span stays UNSET (and, MEDIUM, the call span has no exception event).
- HIGH: `messages.stream()` (3): no tokens on the span. MEDIUM, same scenarios: no finish reason, no output text, no tool call.
- MEDIUM: Responses create (5) and stream (2): no status/finish reason. Responses create and stream: function calls not recorded.
- MEDIUM: chat refusal not recorded.
- Already known: the `messages.stream()` output finding matches open PR https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/180 (issue https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/issues/179). Both Responses tool-call findings match open PR https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/186 (issue https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/issues/185). From its description, PR 180 also covers the `messages.stream()` tokens, finish and tool-call findings (same cause), but the automated title match only marked the output one.

OpenInference findings:
- HIGH: Agents SDK run that raises (5): root span OK.
- HIGH: no span for a chat stream the app closes early, or for a Responses stream ending in an error event.
- MEDIUM: Responses create (5) and stream (2): no status/finish reason.
- MEDIUM: chat refusal not recorded. Not known: the title matcher hit PR 3996, PR 3797 and issue 3785. Read by hand, they are about streamed refusal fragments being overwritten, not a non-streamed refusal going missing. They are recorded as "related".

OpenLLMetry findings:
- HIGH: Agents SDK non-streamed runs (5): two LLM spans per model call (Agents SDK and OpenAI instrumentations), doubling calls and tokens.
- HIGH: Agents SDK run that raises (5): root span OK.
- HIGH: chat streams that raised (error event, cut) and the Responses error-event stream: top-level span OK; MEDIUM, the call span is OK with no exception event.
- HIGH: no span for an Anthropic stream that errors or drops mid-stream (2).
- HIGH: streamed Anthropic spans record 4 output tokens where the provider sent 3 (4). Already known: open PR https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry/pull/4377 describes this exact double count (`message_start` added to the running total in `message_delta`).
- MEDIUM: unknown tool name in an Agents SDK run is on no span.
- Title matches read by hand and rejected: issue 4536 (spans not ended when the app stops reading early; ours is no span after an error or cut), and PRs 4461 and 4462 (reasoning tokens). Token findings now ignore titles about reasoning tokens.

Limits: rule 6 passed for most findings because another library got the same scenario right. Three groups, the Agents SDK root status in each library, rely on the OTel status rule instead, since all three libraries get it wrong. The title matcher in the deduper made 9 matches; 5 were wrong when read by hand; every "already known" above was read by hand.

## 2026-10-10: the planner, the model client and tracing Trueup with neatlogs

- `trueup plan <lib>` asks `claude-sonnet-4.6` for new scenarios as JSON and keeps only what code accepts: valid schema, an existing app, a fake behaviour that app's route supports, an app + model pair not yet covered, and expected truth that an untraced run confirms. Rejected proposals go back to the model with the reason, twice at most. Accepted ones are in `scenarios/proposed/<lib>/` and run with `trueup sweep <lib> --proposed [FROM]`.
- Spending guard: the key's spend is read from the proxy before every call; at $15 Trueup stops.
- Trueup's own run is traced to neatlogs: one session per run, one trace per worker. The scenario subprocesses still get no neatlogs key and have export off; an e2e test watches every outgoing connection from a scenario child and sees none.

### Real runs

`trueup plan openllmetry --max 3` (neatlogs session `20261010T234842Z-plan-openllmetry`) and `trueup plan neatlogs --max 3` (session `20261010T235208Z-plan-neatlogs`). The session id is the run id.

| run | proposals | accepted | rejected | model calls | tokens in / out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| openllmetry | 3 | 3 (all after 1-2 revisions) | 0 | 5 | 29,329 / 1,729 |
| neatlogs | 3 | 3 (2 after revisions) | 0 | 4 | 30,972 / 1,529 |

No proposal was finally rejected, but 6 of 9 tries were rejected first. Reasons: `expected.exception` missing when outcome is exception (4; my first prompt told the model to leave out fields when unsure, and it was not told this one is required), wrong exception class (3: guessed `APIStatusError` or `APIConnectionError`; the untraced run gave `BadRequestError`, `APIConnectionError` and `RemoteProtocolError`), and wrong fake outcome (1: guessed `error_event`; the fake answered HTTP 400 because the app does not stream).

Cost: the per-run spend deltas were $0.0909 and $0.1000. The key's total spend after both runs is $0.2528. The extra $0.06 showed up between and after the runs, when Trueup made no model call, so the proxy's spend figure lags. Tokens at Sonnet list prices ($3 / $15 per million) come to about $0.23, which matches the total. The per-run `run_cost_usd` in `spend.json` reads low for this reason.

Two problems in the planner's output, both fixed:
- `p-an-async-stream-error` said "async anthropic stream", but `an_async_create` does not stream; with the error-event fake model the fake answers HTTP 400. The truth was right (the untraced run confirmed it); only the prose was wrong. Code cannot check prose. I corrected its `does` by hand (the file says so), and the prompt now gives each app's real description. The neatlogs run's descriptions were accurate.
- `p-oa-chat-async-stream-error` caused a false "library changed the request" note: the proposal had `tokens: [null]` and no `include_usage`, so the comparer assumed the app did not ask for usage. The planner now copies `include_usage` from the untraced run (no library there) into accepted chat proposals.

Accepted scenarios: openllmetry `p-an-async-stream-error`, `p-an-stream-helper-error-event`, `p-oa-chat-async-stream-error`; neatlogs `p-an-async-stream-cut`, `p-an-stream-helper-cut`, `p-lc-tools`.

### Leads and findings from them

1	Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.
2	
3	## What it does
4	
5	Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.
6	
7	Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.
8	
9	The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.
10	
11	## Status: early build
12	
13	`trueup doctor`, `trueup sweep <neatlogs|openinference|openllmetry>`, `trueup audit <script> --library <lib>`, `trueup check <run_id|latest> --library <lib>` and `trueup plan <lib> [--max N]` work.
14	
15	`sweep` runs the scenarios (plain SDK, LangChain/LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK; pick with `--framework`) against a fake provider, compares truth with the trace, prints a table of leads and writes truth, trace and `leads.json` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace; it is not a confirmed bug.
16	
17	`audit` runs your script's `main()` against the fake (through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) under the chosen library, once per fake scenario on each provider route the script calls, and compares the same way. It needs a `main()` with no arguments that uses the `openai` or `anthropic` SDK; see `src/trueup/audit.py` for its limits.
18	
19	`check` runs the checker over a sweep's leads. A lead becomes a finding only if it reproduces twice in fresh processes, on the recommended setup, on the latest release and on the library's main branch, the fake really sent what truth says, the harness is sane, another library or the OpenTelemetry conventions show the right behaviour, and a repro under 40 lines shows it. Otherwise it is withdrawn with the rule that failed (kept and counted). Findings that share a cause are grouped, then searched for in the library's GitHub issues and PRs (read only). It writes `findings.json` and `withdrawn.json` in the run dir.
20	
21	`plan` asks a model (`claude-sonnet-4.6` through an OpenAI-compatible proxy) for new scenarios, given the library's wrapper source, the scenario library and the latest findings. A proposal is JSON data: an existing app plus an existing fake behaviour, with the truth it expects. Code checks the schema, that the app and fake behaviour exist and fit, that the pair is new, and runs the app untraced to confirm the truth. A rejected proposal goes back to the model with the reason, twice at most. Accepted ones are saved to `scenarios/proposed/<lib>/`; `trueup sweep <lib> --proposed [FROM]` runs them. Before every model call Trueup reads the key's spend from the proxy and stops at $15. It needs `TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY` and `TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL`.
22	
23	Commands that call the model trace Trueup itself to neatlogs when `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set: one session per run (session id = run id), one trace per worker. The scenario runs stay local: their subprocesses get no neatlogs key and have export turned off.
24	
25	`doctor` also makes one GET each to neatlogs and the model proxy (no model call).
26	
27	The other commands (`fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.
28	
29	Exit codes: 0 no leads, 1 leads found, 2 could not run.

"""Command line entry point."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Sequence

from trueup.runner.setups import LIBRARIES

# Exit codes
EXIT_OK = 0  # no mismatches
EXIT_MISMATCH = 1  # mismatches found
EXIT_ERROR = 2  # could not run

KEY_VARS = ("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "NEATLOGS_PROJECT", "TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY", "TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL")
NOT_BUILT = ("fix", "upstream", "verify", "report")
NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT = "https://ingest.neatlogs.com"


def doctor(http_get: Callable[..., Any] | None = None) -> int:
    ok = sys.version_info >= (3, 12)
    v = sys.version_info
    print(f"python: {v.major}.{v.minor}.{v.micro} ({'ok' if ok else 'need 3.12+'})")
    for name in KEY_VARS:
        # Only report presence. Never print the value.
        state = "set" if os.environ.get(name) else "not set"
        print(f"{name}: {state}")
    print(f"neatlogs: {reach_neatlogs(http_get)}")
    print(f"model proxy: {reach_model(http_get)}")
    return EXIT_OK if ok else EXIT_ERROR


def _get(http_get: Callable[..., Any] | None, url: str, **kw: Any) -> Any:
    import httpx

    kw.setdefault("timeout", 10)
    return (http_get or httpx.get)(url, **kw)


def reach_neatlogs(http_get: Callable[..., Any] | None = None) -> str:
    """One GET to the neatlogs ingest endpoint. Any HTTP reply means reachable."""
    url = os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT") or NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT
    try:
        return f"reachable (HTTP {_get(http_get, url).status_code})"
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"not reachable ({type(e).__name__})"


def reach_model(http_get: Callable[..., Any] | None = None) -> str:
    """One GET to <proxy>/key/info (no model call): reachable, key accepted, spend against the limit."""
    from trueup.model import BASE_VAR, KEY_VAR, SPEND_LIMIT, ModelError, get_spend

    if not os.environ.get(BASE_VAR) or not os.environ.get(KEY_VAR):
        return f"not checked ({BASE_VAR} or {KEY_VAR} not set)"
    try:
        spend = get_spend(os.environ[BASE_VAR], os.environ[KEY_VAR], lambda u, **kw: _get(http_get, u, **kw))
    except ModelError as e:
        return f"reachable, but {e}"
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"not reachable ({type(e).__name__})"
    return f"reachable, key spend ${spend:.4f} of ${SPEND_LIMIT:.2f} limit"


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="trueup",
        description="Find where AI agent traces disagree with what really happened.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in NOT_BUILT:
        sub.add_parser(name, help="not built yet")
    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="check the local setup")
    sw = sub.add_parser("sweep", help="run the scenarios against one tracing library")
    sw.add_argument("library", choices=LIBRARIES)
    sw.add_argument("--framework", default="all", choices=("all", "none", "langchain", "openai-agents"),
                    help="none: plain SDK; langchain: LangChain and LangGraph; default all")
    sw.add_argument("--proposed", nargs="?", const="", metavar="FROM",
                    help="sweep accepted planner proposals from scenarios/proposed/<FROM> (default: this library)")
    pl = sub.add_parser("plan", help="ask the model for new scenarios (data only), keep the ones code accepts")
    pl.add_argument("library", choices=LIBRARIES)
    pl.add_argument("--max", type=int, default=5, help="most proposals to ask for (default 5)")
    au = sub.add_parser("audit", help="run your script's main() against the fake provider and compare its trace")
    au.add_argument("script", type=Path, help="Python file with a main() that calls the openai or anthropic SDK")
    au.add_argument("--library", required=True, choices=LIBRARIES, help="tracing library to set up")
    ck = sub.add_parser("check", help="run the checker and dedupe over a sweep's leads")
    ck.add_argument("run_id", help="a run id under .trueup/runs, or latest")
    ck.add_argument("--library", choices=LIBRARIES, help="with latest: the newest sweep of this library")
    return parser


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "doctor":
        return doctor()
    if args.command == "sweep":
        from trueup.sweep import exit_code, sweep

        proposed = None if args.proposed is None else (args.proposed or args.library)
        if proposed is not None and proposed not in LIBRARIES:
            print(f"trueup sweep: --proposed must name a library: {', '.join(LIBRARIES)}", file=sys.stderr)
            return EXIT_ERROR
        _, results = sweep(Path.cwd(), args.library, args.framework, proposed=proposed)
        return exit_code(results)
    if args.command == "plan":
        return plan_command(args.library, args.max)
    if args.command == "audit":
        from trueup.audit import audit
        from trueup.sweep import exit_code

        _, results = audit(Path.cwd(), args.library, args.script)
        return exit_code(results)
    if args.command == "check":
        from trueup.check import check

        try:
            res = check(Path.cwd(), args.run_id, args.library)
        except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
            print(f"trueup check: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return EXIT_ERROR
        return EXIT_MISMATCH if res["counts"]["findings"] else EXIT_OK
    print(f"trueup {args.command}: not built yet", file=sys.stderr)
    return EXIT_ERROR


def plan_command(library: str, max_n: int) -> int:
    from trueup import tracing
    from trueup.model import ModelError
    from trueup.planner import plan
    from trueup.sweep import new_run_id

    run_id = new_run_id(f"plan-{library}")

    def body() -> int:
        try:
            res = plan(Path.cwd(), library, max_n, run_id=run_id)
        except (ModelError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
            print(f"trueup plan: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return EXIT_ERROR
        return EXIT_ERROR if res["error"] else EXIT_OK

    return tracing.run_traced(run_id, library, "plan", body)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
"""The one model client: the openai SDK against an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM proxy.

Every call first asks the proxy what the key has spent (GET <base>/key/info) and
refuses to call at or above SPEND_LIMIT. The key and base URL come from
TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY and TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL and are never printed or written.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

import httpx

PLAN_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4.6"  # planning and fixing
CHEAP_MODEL = "claude-haiku"  # cheap jobs
SPEND_LIMIT = 15.0  # USD, from the key's spend on the proxy
KEY_VAR, BASE_VAR = "TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY", "TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL"


class ModelError(RuntimeError):
    """The model could not give a usable answer. Stops the worker that asked."""


class SpendLimitReached(ModelError):
    """The key has spent SPEND_LIMIT or more. No call is made."""


def check_model(name: str) -> str:
    if "opus" in name.lower():
        raise ModelError(f"model {name!r} is not allowed (no opus models)")
    return name


def proxy_root(base_url: str) -> str:
    """The proxy's root: the base URL without a trailing /v1."""
    b = base_url.rstrip("/")
    return b[: -len("/v1")] if b.endswith("/v1") else b


def get_spend(base_url: str, key: str, http_get: Callable[..., Any] = httpx.get) -> float:
    """The key's spend in USD, read from info.spend of GET <root>/key/info."""
    r = http_get(proxy_root(base_url) + "/key/info", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=20)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise ModelError(f"could not read the key's spend: HTTP {r.status_code}")
    try:
        return float(r.json()["info"]["spend"] or 0.0)
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as e:
        raise ModelError(f"could not read the key's spend: no info.spend in the reply ({type(e).__name__})") from None


def guard(spend: float, limit: float = SPEND_LIMIT) -> None:
    if spend >= limit:
        raise SpendLimitReached(f"spend limit reached: the key has spent ${spend:.4f}, limit ${limit:.2f}. "
                                "No model call made.")


def parse_json(text: str) -> Any:
    """JSON from a model reply; a ```json fence around it is allowed."""
    t = text.strip()
    m = re.fullmatch(r"```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```", t, re.S)
    return json.loads(m.group(1) if m else t)


@dataclass
class Usage:
    calls: int = 0
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    by_model: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def add(self, model: str, inp: int, out: int) -> None:
        self.calls += 1
        self.input_tokens += inp
        self.output_tokens += out
        m = self.by_model.setdefault(model, {"calls": 0, "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0})
        m["calls"] += 1
        m["input_tokens"] += inp
        m["output_tokens"] += out

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"calls": self.calls, "input_tokens": self.input_tokens, "output_tokens": self.output_tokens,
                "by_model": self.by_model}


class ModelClient:
    def __init__(self, key: str | None = None, base_url: str | None = None, *, limit: float = SPEND_LIMIT,
                 retries: int = 3, json_retries: int = 2, backoff: float = 2.0,
                 http_get: Callable[..., Any] = httpx.get, openai_client: Any = None,
                 sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep) -> None:
        self.key = key or os.environ.get(KEY_VAR) or ""
        self.base_url = base_url or os.environ.get(BASE_VAR) or ""
        if not self.key or not self.base_url:
            raise ModelError(f"{KEY_VAR} and {BASE_VAR} must be set")
        self.limit, self.retries, self.json_retries, self.backoff = limit, retries, json_retries, backoff
        self.http_get, self.sleep = http_get, sleep
        self.usage = Usage()
        if openai_client is None:
            import openai

            openai_client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=self.key, base_url=self.base_url, max_retries=0, timeout=180)
        self.client = openai_client

    def spend(self) -> float:
        return get_spend(self.base_url, self.key, self.http_get)

    def chat(self, model: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], max_tokens: int = 4000) -> str:
        """One completion, after the spend guard, with retries and backoff on API errors."""
        import openai

        check_model(model)
        last: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):
            guard(self.spend(), self.limit)
            try:
                r = self.client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                                        temperature=0.2)
            except (openai.APIConnectionError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.RateLimitError,
                    openai.InternalServerError) as e:
                last = e
                if attempt < self.retries:
                    self.sleep(self.backoff * 2 ** attempt)
                continue
            except openai.APIStatusError as e:  # 4xx other than 429: retrying will not help
                raise ModelError(f"model call failed: HTTP {e.status_code}") from None
            u = r.usage
            self.usage.add(model, getattr(u, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0, getattr(u, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0)
            return r.choices[0].message.content or ""
        raise ModelError(f"model call failed after {self.retries + 1} tries: {type(last).__name__}")

    def chat_json(self, model: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], max_tokens: int = 4000) -> Any:
        """Like chat, but the reply must be JSON. Invalid JSON is retried, then raises ModelError."""
        msgs = list(messages)
        for attempt in range(self.json_retries + 1):
            text = self.chat(model, msgs, max_tokens)
            try:
                return parse_json(text)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                msgs = [*messages, {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                        {"role": "user", "content": f"That was not valid JSON ({e.msg}). Reply with JSON only."}]
        raise ModelError(f"model {model} gave invalid JSON {self.json_retries + 1} times; stopping this worker")


def record_spend(run_dir: Path, name: str, client: ModelClient) -> float | None:
    """Write the key's spend to <run_dir>/spend.json under `name` (before/after). None if unreadable."""
    path = run_dir / "spend.json"
    data = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
    try:
        spend: float | None = client.spend()
        data[name] = {"spend_usd": spend, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())}
    except ModelError as e:
        spend = None
        data[name] = {"error": str(e)}
    if name == "after":
        data["usage"] = client.usage.to_dict()
        if data.get("before", {}).get("spend_usd") is not None and spend is not None:
            data["run_cost_usd"] = round(spend - data["before"]["spend_usd"], 6)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1))
    return spend
"""Trueup traces itself with neatlogs.

One trueup run = one neatlogs session (session id = run id). Each worker runs as
its own root trace named after it (trueup-planner, trueup-runner, ...), with
trueup.run_id, trueup.library and, where it applies, trueup.verdict.

This is the outer trace only. Scenario runs happen in subprocesses whose env
drops NEATLOGS_API_KEY and sets NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT / OTEL_*_EXPORTER=none
(trueup.runner.setups), so their spans never leave the machine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import atexit
import contextlib
import os
import sys
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator

from trueup import __version__

KEY_VAR = "NEATLOGS_API_KEY"
WORKERS = ("trueup-planner", "trueup-runner", "trueup-comparer", "trueup-checker", "trueup-deduper")

_state: dict[str, Any] = {"active": False, "run_id": None, "library": None, "flushed": False}


def active() -> bool:
    return bool(_state["active"])


def session_id() -> str | None:
    return _state["run_id"] if active() else None


def start(run_id: str, library: str, command: str, out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
          init: Callable[..., Any] | None = None) -> bool:
    """neatlogs.init for a command that calls the model. Returns whether tracing is on."""
    _state.update(active=False, run_id=run_id, library=library, flushed=False)
    if not os.environ.get(KEY_VAR):
        out(f"{KEY_VAR} is not set: running without neatlogs tracing")
        return False
    if init is None:
        import neatlogs

        init = neatlogs.init
    try:
        init(api_key=os.environ[KEY_VAR], workflow_name="trueup", instrumentations=["openai"],
             tags=[f"run_id:{run_id}", f"library:{library}", f"trueup:{__version__}", f"command:{command}"])
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - tracing must not stop the run
        out(f"neatlogs init failed ({type(e).__name__}): running without neatlogs tracing")
        return False
    _state["active"] = True
    atexit.register(flush)
    out(f"neatlogs tracing on, session {run_id}")
    return True


def flush() -> None:
    """Flush neatlogs once. Safe to call more than once and when tracing is off."""
    if not active() or _state["flushed"]:
        return
    _state["flushed"] = True
    try:
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.flush()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"neatlogs flush failed ({type(e).__name__})", file=sys.stderr)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def worker(name: str, **attrs: Any) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """A root trace for one worker in the run's session. Yields a span (or None when off)."""
    if name not in WORKERS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown worker {name!r}")
    if not active():
        yield None
        return
    import neatlogs

    a = {"trueup.run_id": _state["run_id"], "trueup.library": _state["library"], "neatlogs.workflow.name": name,
         **{f"trueup.{k}": v for k, v in attrs.items()}}
    with neatlogs.trace(name=name, kind="AGENT", session_id=_state["run_id"], **a):
        from opentelemetry import trace as otel

        yield otel.get_current_span()


def set_verdict(span: Any, verdict: str) -> None:
    if span is not None:
        span.set_attribute("trueup.verdict", verdict)


def run_traced(run_id: str, library: str, command: str, body: Callable[[], int],
               out: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> int:
    """Start tracing, run the command, and flush on the way out, also when it raises."""
    start(run_id, library, command, out)
    try:
        return body()
    finally:
        flush()

"""trueup plan <library> [--max N]: the model proposes new scenarios as data; code decides.

The planner reads the library's wrapper source from its venv, the scenario
library and the latest findings, and asks the model for new scenarios as JSON.
Every proposal is checked by trueup.scenarios.proposed (schema, app and fake
behaviour exist, truth matches an untraced run). A rejected proposal goes back
to the model with the reason, at most REVISIONS times. Accepted ones are saved
to scenarios/proposed/<library>/ for `trueup sweep <library> --proposed`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.model import PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, record_spend
from trueup.scenarios import ALL
from trueup.scenarios import proposed as prop

REVISIONS = 2
SOURCE_LIMIT = 60_000  # characters of wrapper source sent to the model
FILE_LIMIT = 32_000

# Wrapper files per library, relative to site-packages, most relevant first.
WRAPPER_FILES = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs/openai.py", "neatlogs/anthropic.py"],
    "openllmetry": ["opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/shared/chat_wrappers.py",
                    "opentelemetry/instrumentation/anthropic/streaming.py",
                    "opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/v1/responses_wrappers.py"],
    "openinference": ["openinference/instrumentation/openai/_stream.py",
                      "openinference/instrumentation/openai/_request.py",
                      "openinference/instrumentation/anthropic/_stream.py"],
}

SYSTEM = """You plan test scenarios for Trueup, which checks whether an AI tracing library's spans match \
what really happened. A scenario runs one existing app function against a fake provider; the fake model name \
picks the fake's behaviour. You cannot write code: a scenario is JSON data that combines an existing app with an \
existing fake model, plus the truth you expect the run to produce.

Propose scenarios that are NEW (an app + fake model pair not already in the library) and likely to expose a \
tracing bug, given the wrapper source: code paths the existing scenarios miss (a different app reading style on \
the same failure, streaming vs non-streaming, async, tools with errors, refusal through streaming, ...).

Expected truth fields (only listed ones are checked, against what the fake really did):
  calls: number of requests the fake received
  outcome: "ok" or "exception" (what the app saw); exception: the exception class name when outcome is exception
  fake: per call, what the fake did: complete, failed, incomplete, error_event, cut, http_error
  tokens: per call {"input": n, "output": n}, or null when the fake sent no usage
  finish: per call, list of finish reasons / response status
  tool_calls: per call, list of tool names the model asked for
  tool_runs: framework apps only, [{"name", "outcome": "ok"|"raised"}]
  include_usage: per call, whether the app's request asked for stream usage
Facts about the fake: OpenAI replies use 11 input / 7 output tokens, Anthropic 5 / 3. Streams send usage only \
when the app asks (include_usage) on chat; Responses and Anthropic streams always send it. Leave out a field \
when unsure rather than guess; calls, outcome and fake are required, and exception is required when outcome is \
"exception". Each app's "e.g." is what an existing scenario with it does: keep "does" true to the app (an app \
that does not stream does not stream, whatever the fake model).

Reply with JSON only, no prose: {"proposals": [{"id": "p-...", "provider", "api", "framework", "does", "app", \
"model", "expected": {...}, "rationale": "why a wrapper might get this wrong"}]}"""


def wrapper_source(root: Path, library: str) -> str:
    site = next((root / ".trueup" / "venvs" / library / "lib").glob("python*/site-packages"), None)
    if site is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no venv for {library}; run `trueup sweep {library}` first")
    parts, total = [], 0
    for rel in WRAPPER_FILES[library]:
        f = site / rel
        if not f.exists() or total >= SOURCE_LIMIT:
            continue
        text = f.read_text()[: min(FILE_LIMIT, SOURCE_LIMIT - total)]
        total += len(text)
        parts.append(f"### {rel}\n{text}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def latest_findings(root: Path, library: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    runs = sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob(f"*-{library}/findings.json"))
    if not runs:
        return []
    d = json.loads(runs[-1].read_text())
    out = [{"title": f["title"], "severity": f["severity"], "check": f["details"]["check"],
            "scenarios": f["details"]["scenarios"]} for f in d["findings"]]
    out += [{"title": f.get("title"), "verdict": "disputed"} for f in d.get("disputed_semantics", [])]
    return out


def library_summary() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [{"id": s.id, "app": s.app, "model": s.model, "framework": s.framework} for s in ALL] + [
        {"id": s.id, "app": s.app, "model": s.model, "framework": s.framework, "proposed": True}
        for s in prop.load()]


def first_prompt(library: str, source: str, findings: list[dict[str, Any]], n: int) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    user = (f"Library under test: {library}.\n\nWhat a scenario may use:\n{json.dumps(prop.catalogue())}\n\n"
            f"Existing scenarios (do not repeat an app + model pair):\n{json.dumps(library_summary())}\n\n"
            f"Current findings for {library}:\n{json.dumps(findings)}\n\n"
            f"Wrapper source of {library} as installed:\n{source}\n\nPropose at most {n} new scenarios.")
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def revision_prompt(p: Any, reasons: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    user = (f"What a scenario may use:\n{json.dumps(prop.catalogue())}\n\nExisting app + model pairs:\n"
            f"{json.dumps(sorted({f'{s.app}+{s.model}' for s in ALL}))}\n\nYour proposal:\n{json.dumps(p)}\n\n"
            "It was rejected:\n- " + "\n- ".join(reasons) +
            '\n\nFix it and reply with JSON only: {"proposals": [<the one fixed proposal>]}.'
            ' Reply {"proposals": []} to withdraw it.')
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def check(p: Any, taken: set[tuple[str, str]], ids: set[str],
          untraced: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], tuple[list[str], Any]]) -> list[str]:
    reasons = prop.validate(p, taken, ids)
    if reasons:
        return reasons
    diffs, truth = untraced(p)
    if not diffs and truth and p["api"] == "chat" and "include_usage" not in p["expected"]:
        # The untraced run has no library, so its request shows what the app itself asks for.
        # Without this the comparer guesses from tokens and can report a library change that is not one.
        p["expected"]["include_usage"] = truth["include_usage"]
    return diffs


def plan(root: Path, library: str, max_n: int = 5, *, client: ModelClient | None = None,
         run_id: str | None = None, out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
         untraced: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], tuple[list[str], Any]] = prop.untraced_check,
         save: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from trueup.sweep import new_run_id

    run_id = run_id or new_run_id(f"plan-{library}")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = client or ModelClient()
    record_spend(run_dir, "before", client)
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"run_id": run_id, "library": library, "model": PLAN_MODEL, "max": max_n,
                              "session_id": tracing.session_id(), "proposals": [], "accepted": [], "rejected": [],
                              "error": None}
    try:
        with tracing.worker("trueup-planner") as span:
            _plan(root, library, max_n, client, result, out, untraced, save)
            tracing.set_verdict(span, f"accepted {len(result['accepted'])}, rejected {len(result['rejected'])}")
    except ModelError as e:
        result["error"] = str(e)
        out(f"planner stopped: {e}")
    finally:
        record_spend(run_dir, "after", client)
        spend = json.loads((run_dir / "spend.json").read_text())
        result["usage"], result["cost_usd"] = spend.get("usage"), spend.get("run_cost_usd")
        (run_dir / "plan.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1, default=str))
    out(f"proposals: {len(result['proposals'])}  accepted: {len(result['accepted'])}  "
        f"rejected: {len(result['rejected'])}")
    for r in result["rejected"]:
        out(f"  rejected {r['id']}: {'; '.join(r['reasons'])}")
    out(f"tokens: {client.usage.input_tokens} in, {client.usage.output_tokens} out; "
        f"cost ${result['cost_usd'] if result['cost_usd'] is not None else '?'}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return result


def _plan(root: Path, library: str, max_n: int, client: ModelClient, result: dict[str, Any],
          out: Callable[[str], None], untraced: Callable[..., Any], save: bool) -> None:
    source = wrapper_source(root, library)
    findings = latest_findings(root, library)
    out(f"planning for {library}: {len(source)} chars of wrapper source, {len(findings)} findings")
    reply = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, first_prompt(library, source, findings, max_n))
    props = reply.get("proposals") if isinstance(reply, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(props, list):
        raise ModelError('model reply has no "proposals" list; stopping the planner')
    existing = prop.load()
    taken = {(s.app, s.model) for s in existing}
    ids = {s.id for s in existing}
    for p in props[:max_n]:
        result["proposals"].append(p)
        pid = p.get("id", "?") if isinstance(p, dict) else "?"
        history = []
        for attempt in range(REVISIONS + 1):
            reasons = check(p, taken, ids, untraced)
            if not reasons:
                break
            history.append({"proposal": p, "reasons": reasons})
            out(f"  {pid}: rejected ({'; '.join(reasons)[:200]})")
            if attempt == REVISIONS:
                break
            rev = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, revision_prompt(p, reasons))
            revised = rev.get("proposals") if isinstance(rev, dict) else None
            if not revised:
                history.append({"proposal": None, "reasons": ["withdrawn by the model"]})
                reasons = ["withdrawn by the model after: " + "; ".join(reasons)]
                break
            p = revised[0]
        if reasons:
            result["rejected"].append({"id": pid, "reasons": reasons, "tries": len(history), "history": history})
            continue
        taken.add((p["app"], p["model"]))
        ids.add(p["id"])
        path = prop.save(p, library) if save else None
        result["accepted"].append({"id": p["id"], "revisions": len(history), "proposal": p,
                                   "path": str(path) if path else None})
        out(f"  {p['id']}: accepted{f' after {len(history)} revision(s)' if history else ''}")
"""Per-library venvs under .trueup/venvs/<lib>, built with uv."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from trueup.runner.setups import PACKAGES

STAMP = "trueup-packages.json"


class VenvError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def venv_dir(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return root.resolve() / ".trueup" / "venvs" / library


def python_path(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return venv_dir(root, library) / "bin" / "python"


def is_ready(root: Path, library: str) -> bool:
    stamp = venv_dir(root, library) / STAMP
    if not stamp.exists() or not python_path(root, library).exists():
        return False
    try:
        return json.loads(stamp.read_text()) == PACKAGES[library]
    except ValueError:
        return False


def ensure(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 900) -> Path:
    """Create the venv if missing or out of date. Returns its python."""
    if library not in PACKAGES:
        raise VenvError(f"unknown library {library!r}")
    py = python_path(root, library)
    if is_ready(root, library):
        return py
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if uv is None:
        raise VenvError("uv not found on PATH")
    d = venv_dir(root, library)
    d.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    steps = [
        [uv, "venv", "--quiet", "--allow-existing", "--python", "3.12", str(d)],
        [uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--python", str(py), *PACKAGES[library]],
    ]
    for cmd in steps:
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            raise VenvError(f"timed out: {' '.join(cmd[:3])}") from None
        if p.returncode != 0:
            raise VenvError(f"{' '.join(cmd[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-500:]}")
    (d / STAMP).write_text(json.dumps(PACKAGES[library]))
    return py


def _run(cmd: list[str], timeout: float, cwd: Path | None = None) -> str:
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        raise VenvError(f"timed out: {' '.join(cmd[:3])}") from None
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise VenvError(f"{' '.join(cmd[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-500:]}")
    return p.stdout


def upgrade(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 900) -> Path:
    """Bring the library's venv to the latest releases on PyPI. Returns its python."""
    py = ensure(root, library, timeout)
    uv = shutil.which("uv") or "uv"
    _run([uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--upgrade", "--python", str(py), *PACKAGES[library]], timeout)
    return py


# The library's main branch: repo, and local package paths that replace PyPI distributions.
MAIN_SOURCES: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {
    "neatlogs": {"repo": "https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs", "paths": {"neatlogs": "."}},
    "openinference": {
        "repo": "https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference",
        "paths": {
            "openinference-semantic-conventions": "python/openinference-semantic-conventions",
            "openinference-instrumentation": "python/openinference-instrumentation",
            **{f"openinference-instrumentation-{n}": f"python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-{n}"
               for n in ("openai", "anthropic", "langchain", "openai-agents")},
        },
    },
    "openllmetry": {
        "repo": "https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry",
        "paths": {
            "opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai": "packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai",
            **{f"opentelemetry-instrumentation-{n}": f"packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-{n}"
               for n in ("openai", "anthropic", "langchain", "openai-agents")},
            "traceloop-sdk": "packages/traceloop-sdk",
        },
    },
}


def clone_dir(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return root.resolve() / ".trueup" / "src" / str(MAIN_SOURCES[library]["repo"]).rsplit("/", 1)[1]


def ensure_main(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 1200) -> tuple[Path, str]:
    """Shallow-clone main and install its packages into .trueup/venvs/<lib>-main. Returns (python, commit)."""
    src = MAIN_SOURCES[library]
    paths: dict[str, str] = src["paths"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
    clone = clone_dir(root, library)
    git = shutil.which("git") or "git"
    if not (clone / ".git").exists():
        clone.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _run([git, "clone", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", str(src["repo"]), str(clone)], timeout)
    commit = _run([git, "-C", str(clone), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], 60).strip()
    d = venv_dir(root, f"{library}-main")
    py = d / "bin" / "python"
    stamp = {"commit": commit, "packages": PACKAGES[library]}
    if py.exists() and (d / STAMP).exists() and json.loads((d / STAMP).read_text()) == stamp:
        return py, commit
    uv = shutil.which("uv") or "uv"
    pypi = [p for p in PACKAGES[library] if p not in paths]
    _run([uv, "venv", "--quiet", "--allow-existing", "--python", "3.12", str(d)], timeout)
    _run([uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--python", str(py), *pypi, *(str(clone / p) for p in paths.values())],
         timeout)
    (d / STAMP).write_text(json.dumps(stamp))
    return py, commit
"""Parent side: run one scenario in a fresh subprocess and read its observation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from trueup.runner.setups import CHILD_ENV, CHILD_ENV_DROP
from trueup.scenarios import BUILT, get

SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]  # .../src
RAN = "ran"
NOT_RUN = "not_run"


def child_env(base: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = dict(os.environ if base is None else base)
    for k in CHILD_ENV_DROP:
        env.pop(k, None)
    env.update(CHILD_ENV)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(SRC)
    env.pop("VIRTUAL_ENV", None)
    return env


def not_run(scenario_id: str, library: str, reason: str, seconds: float = 0.0, detail: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"scenario": scenario_id, "library": library, "status": NOT_RUN, "reason": reason,
            "detail": detail, "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "observation": None}


def _last_line(text: str) -> str:
    lines = [ln for ln in text.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines[-1].strip() if lines else "no output"


def run_scenario(python: Path, library: str, scenario_id: str, timeout: float = 90) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns {scenario, library, status, reason, seconds, observation}."""
    try:
        scenario = get(scenario_id)
    except KeyError as e:
        return not_run(scenario_id, library, str(e))
    if scenario.status != BUILT:
        return not_run(scenario_id, library, f"scenario is {scenario.status}")
    return _run_child(python, library, scenario_id, [library, scenario_id], timeout)


def run_audit(python: Path, library: str, script: Path, label: str, overrides: dict[str, str],
              timeout: float = 90) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a user's script's main() with the fake answering as `overrides` say. Same shape as run_scenario."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-") as tmp:
        ov = Path(tmp) / "overrides.json"
        ov.write_text(json.dumps(overrides))
        return _run_child(python, library, label, ["--audit", library, str(script.resolve()), str(ov)], timeout)


def _run_child(python: Path, library: str, label: str, args: list[str], timeout: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-") as tmp:
        out = Path(tmp) / "obs.json"
        cmd = [str(python), "-m", "trueup.runner.child", *args, str(out)]
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, env=child_env(), cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return not_run(label, library, f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s", time.monotonic() - t0)
        except OSError as e:
            return not_run(label, library, f"could not start {python}: {e}")
        seconds = time.monotonic() - t0
        if not out.exists():
            tail = (p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-2000:]
            return not_run(label, library, f"child exited {p.returncode} without output: {_last_line(tail)}",
                           seconds, detail=tail)
        payload = json.loads(out.read_text())
    if not payload["ok"]:
        return not_run(label, library, "setup or harness error: " + _last_line(payload["error"]), seconds,
                       detail=payload["error"])
    return {"scenario": label, "library": library, "status": RAN, "reason": None,
            "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "observation": payload["observation"]}
"""trueup sweep <library> [--framework ...]: run the scenarios against one library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.core import report
from trueup.core.compare import compare, leads
from trueup.core.model import Mismatch, Observation
from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario, venvs
from trueup.runner.run import not_run
from trueup.scenarios import FRAMEWORKS, select
from trueup.scenarios.proposed import load as load_proposed


def new_run_id(library: str) -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ") + f"-{library}"


def summary_line(r: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    sid = r["scenario"]
    if r["status"] != RAN:
        return f"{sid:30} NOT RUN  {r['reason']}"
    t, tr = r["observation"]["truth"], r["observation"]["trace"]
    app = t["app"]["outcome"] if t["outcome"] == "ok" else f"raised {t['exception']}"
    spans = ", ".join(f"{s['name']}={s['status']['code']}" for s in tr["spans"]) or "none"
    line = f"{sid:30} ran {r['seconds']:5.1f}s  app {app}; fake calls {t['calls']}; spans {len(tr['spans'])}: {spans}"
    if t.get("expected_mismatch"):
        line += f"  [truth differs from scenario expectation: {', '.join(t['expected_mismatch'])}]"
    return line


def sweep(
    root: Path,
    library: str,
    framework: str = "all",
    *,
    proposed: str | None = None,
    ensure: Callable[[Path, str], Path] = venvs.ensure,
    run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_scenario,
    out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
) -> tuple[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    run_id = new_run_id(library) + ("-proposed" if proposed else "")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    started = time.monotonic()
    scenarios = select(framework) if proposed is None else [
        s for s in load_proposed(proposed) if framework == "all" or s.framework in FRAMEWORKS[framework]]
    try:
        out(f"preparing venv for {library}")
        python: Path | None = ensure(root, library)
        venv_error = None
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - every scenario is reported NOT RUN
        python, venv_error = None, f"venv not ready: {e}"
    results = []
    with tracing.worker("trueup-runner") as span:
        for s in scenarios:
            r = not_run(s.id, library, venv_error) if python is None else run(python, library, s.id)
            results.append(r)
            out(summary_line(r))
        tracing.set_verdict(span, f"ran {sum(r['status'] == RAN for r in results)}/{len(results)}")
    with tracing.worker("trueup-comparer") as span:
        for r in results:
            if r["status"] == RAN:
                r["mismatches"] = [m.to_dict() for m in compare(Observation.from_dict(r["observation"]))]
            (run_dir / f"{r['scenario']}.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1, default=str))
        n = sum(len(leads([Mismatch.from_dict(m) for m in r.get("mismatches", [])])) for r in results)
        tracing.set_verdict(span, f"{n} leads")
    ran = sum(r["status"] == RAN for r in results)
    by = by_scenario(results)
    c = report.counts(by)
    table = report.table(by)
    totals = (f"leads: {c['leads']} (high {c['by_severity']['high']}, medium {c['by_severity']['medium']}, "
              f"low {c['by_severity']['low']})  notes: {c['notes']}")
    lines = [
        f"trueup sweep {library} --framework {framework}{f' --proposed {proposed}' if proposed else ''}  run {run_id}",
        f"scenarios: {len(results)}  ran: {ran}  not run: {len(results) - ran}  "
        f"time: {time.monotonic() - started:.0f} s",
        totals,
        "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace, not a confirmed bug.",
        "",
        *(summary_line(r) for r in results),
        "",
        table,
    ]
    (run_dir / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    (run_dir / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "framework": framework,
        "proposed": proposed,
        "scenarios": [{"id": r["scenario"], "status": r["status"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results],
    }, indent=1))
    not_run_list = [{"scenario": r["scenario"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results if r["status"] != RAN]
    (run_dir / "leads.json").write_text(json.dumps(report.leads_payload(run_id, library, by, not_run_list), indent=1,
                                                   default=str))
    out("")
    out(table)
    out(totals)
    out(f"ran {ran}/{len(results)}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return run_dir, results


def by_scenario(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]:
    return [(r["scenario"], [Mismatch.from_dict(m) for m in r.get("mismatches", [])])
            for r in results if r["status"] == RAN]


def exit_code(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """1 if any lead, else 2 if any scenario could not run, else 0."""
    if any(leads([m for _, ms in by_scenario(results) for m in ms])):
        return 1
    return 2 if not results or any(r["status"] == NOT_RUN for r in results) else 0

"""OpenTelemetry OpenAI Agents instrumentation"""

import os
from typing import Collection
from opentelemetry.trace import get_tracer
from opentelemetry.metrics import Meter, get_meter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.instrumentor import BaseInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.openai_agents.version import __version__
from opentelemetry.semconv_ai import Meters


_instruments = ("openai-agents >= 0.2.0",)


class OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor(BaseInstrumentor):
    """An instrumentor for OpenAI Agents SDK."""

    def __init__(self, *, replace_existing_processors: bool = False) -> None:
        """Initialize the instrumentor.

        Args:
            replace_existing_processors:
                If enabled, any existing trace processors
                will be cleared before this processor is added as the only one.
                By default, the openai-agents library has
                a built-in tracing processor that is always active,
                and this processor will be added alongside it,
                resulting in traces being sent to multiple backends.
        """
        super().__init__()
        self._replace_existing_processors: bool = replace_existing_processors

    def instrumentation_dependencies(self) -> Collection[str]:
        return _instruments

    def _instrument(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        """Override the abstract base method and instrument openai-agents.

        Args:
            tracer_provider: An optional TracerProvider to use
                when creating a Tracer.
            meter_provider: An optional MeterProvider to use
                when creating a Meter.

            Additional kwargs are ignored.
        """
        tracer_provider = kwargs.get("tracer_provider")
        tracer = get_tracer(__name__, __version__, tracer_provider)

        meter_provider = kwargs.get("meter_provider")
        meter = get_meter(__name__, __version__, meter_provider)

        if is_metrics_enabled():
            _create_metrics(meter)

        # Use hook-based approach with OpenAI Agents SDK callbacks
        try:
            from agents import add_trace_processor, set_trace_processors
            from ._hooks import OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor

            # Create and add our OpenTelemetry processor
            otel_processor = OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor(tracer)
            if self._replace_existing_processors:
                set_trace_processors([otel_processor])
            else:
                add_trace_processor(otel_processor)

        except Exception:
            # Silently handle import errors - OpenAI Agents SDK may not be available
            pass

        try:
            from ._realtime_wrappers import wrap_realtime_session

            wrap_realtime_session(tracer)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _uninstrument(self, **kwargs):
        try:
            from ._realtime_wrappers import unwrap_realtime_session

            unwrap_realtime_session()
        except Exception:
            pass


def is_metrics_enabled() -> bool:
    return (os.getenv("TRACELOOP_METRICS_ENABLED") or "true").lower() == "true"


def _create_metrics(meter: Meter):
    token_histogram = meter.create_histogram(
        name=Meters.LLM_TOKEN_USAGE,
        unit="token",
        description="Measures number of input and output tokens used",
    )

    duration_histogram = meter.create_histogram(
        name=Meters.LLM_OPERATION_DURATION,
        unit="s",
        description="GenAI operation duration",
    )

    return token_histogram, duration_histogram

        self._tracer = tracer
        # Guards the capped insert into _reverse_handoffs_dict below, which is the only
        # read-modify-write here: every other access to the dicts on this object is a
        # single subscript, pop or get. Those are atomic because every key here is a str,
        # so the operation never re-enters the interpreter to hash or compare -- a key
        # with a Python-level __hash__ or __eq__ would not get that. The SDK invokes these
        # callbacks on whichever thread is running the agent, so a process driving
        # Runner.run_sync from several threads reaches them concurrently.
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        # Spans and traces still in flight, deliberately unbounded. The number of
        # simultaneously open spans scales with how many runs are in flight, so any cap
        # large enough to be safe under load is too large to bound anything, and evicting
        # an open span is far more damaging than leaking a dict entry: the span would be
        # ended early with only its start attributes, its real end would be dropped, and
