"""Generate a minimal repro script for one scenario under one library. Pure: returns text.

The script runs offline: trueup's local fake provider answers, the API keys are
fake placeholders and export is off. It sets up the library the recommended way,
runs the scenario's app, compares truth with the spans and prints each lead as a
JSON line. It needs trueup's src on PYTHONPATH (for the fake and the app code)
and a venv with the library installed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

TEMPLATE = '''"""Repro: {library} on scenario {scenario}. {does}
Offline: a local fake provider answers; no API keys, no network.
Run with {library} installed: PYTHONPATH=<trueup>/src python {filename}
"""
import gc, json, os
from trueup.runner.setups import CHILD_ENV, SETUPS, quiet_agents_sdk
os.environ.update(CHILD_ENV)  # content capture on, export off, fake keys
from trueup.core.compare import compare, leads
from trueup.core.model import Observation
from trueup.fake import FakeProvider
from trueup.runner import framework_apps, truth
from trueup.runner.apps import APPS
from trueup.runner.child import span_to_dict
from trueup.scenarios import get

s = get("{scenario}")
exporter, flush = SETUPS["{library}"](s.framework)  # the library's recommended setup
if s.framework == "openai-agents":
    quiet_agents_sdk()  # drop the Agents SDK's own upload to api.openai.com
with FakeProvider() as fake:
    try:
        app = {{"outcome": "ok", "result": APPS[s.app](fake.base_url, s.model)}}
    except Exception as e:
        app = {{"outcome": "exception", "exception_type": type(e).__name__, "message": str(e)}}
    gc.collect()
    flush()
    log = fake.log.entries()
t = {{**truth.derive(log, app, framework_apps.TOOL_RUNS), "expected": s.expected, "app": app, "fake_log": log}}
spans = [span_to_dict(x) for x in exporter.get_finished_spans()]
for m in leads(compare(Observation(t, {{"library": "{library}", "spans": spans}}))):
    print(json.dumps(m.to_dict(), default=str))
'''


def generate(library: str, scenario: str, does: str) -> str:
    return TEMPLATE.format(library=library, scenario=scenario, does=does.strip(),
                           filename=f"{library}-{scenario}.py")


def line_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(text.rstrip("\n").splitlines())

This module gathers the evidence (the effects); the rules in trueup.core.checker
decide. Steps, one library at a time:
  1. bring the library's venv to the latest release and record versions against PyPI
  2. rerun every scenario with a lead twice, each in a fresh process
  3. build .trueup/venvs/<lib>-main from a shallow clone of main and run the scenarios there
  4. read the other libraries' latest sweeps of the same scenarios (compared again with
     today's adapters)
  5. generate a repro per scenario and run it
  6. apply the rules, group findings by cause, search GitHub for each finding (read only)
Writes findings.json, withdrawn.json and evidence.json next to the sweep's leads.json.
"""

def sweeps(root: Path, library: str | None) -> list[Path]:
    """Sweep run dirs (leads.json, not audits), oldest first. Proposed-scenario sweeps end in -proposed."""
    runs = root / ".trueup" / "runs"
    return sorted(d for d in runs.glob("*") if (d / "leads.json").exists() and "-audit-" not in d.name
                  and (library is None or d.name.endswith((f"-{library}", f"-{library}-proposed"))))

"""Where a finding's code lives in each library, and how that package runs its own tests.

A target is keyed by (library, code path) as the checker groups findings. It names
the packages in the library's repo the fix may touch, the symbols to start the
search from (the wrapper), the symbols that show how the library already gets a
similar case right, and the test requirements of each package.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

REPOS = {
    "neatlogs": "https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs",
    "openinference": "https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference",
    "openllmetry": "https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry",
}

               "openllmetry": "traceloop/openllmetry"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Package:
    path: str  # in the repo
    dist: str  # distribution name, as installed in the scenario venv
    tests: str = "tests"  # relative to path
    # Test requirements: "group:<name>" reads [dependency-groups] of the package's pyproject,
    # "file:<name>" a requirements file in the package; anything else is a requirement.
    test_deps: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # Local packages of the same repo the tests need from source (editable).
    local_deps: tuple[str, ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Target:
    library: str
    code_path: str
    packages: tuple[Package, ...]
    seeds: tuple[str, ...]  # wrapper functions or classes to locate
    reference_seeds: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # where the library gets a similar case right
    reference_note: str = ""  # the rule the fix must follow (OTel GenAI conventions)
    extra: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


_OLL_SEMCONV = "packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai"
_OLL_TEST = ("group:test", "group:dev")
_OI_CORE = ("python/openinference-semantic-conventions", "python/openinference-instrumentation")

TARGETS: dict[tuple[str, str], Target] = {
    ("openllmetry", "openai-agents"): Target(
        library="openllmetry", code_path="openai-agents",
        packages=(
            Package("packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents", "opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents",
                    test_deps=_OLL_TEST, local_deps=(_OLL_SEMCONV, "packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai")),
            Package("packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai", "opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai",
                    test_deps=_OLL_TEST, local_deps=(_OLL_SEMCONV,)),
        ),
        seeds=("OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor", "on_span_start", "on_span_end", "responses_get_or_create_wrapper",
               "async_responses_get_or_create_wrapper"),
        reference_seeds=("SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY",),
        reference_note=("OTel GenAI conventions: one inference span per model call. OpenInference records the "
                        "same Agents SDK runs with one LLM span per call. Inside OpenLLMetry, the LangChain "
                        "instrumentation sets SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY in the context so the "
                        "provider instrumentation under it does not record the same call again."),
    ),
    ("openinference", "openai-agents"): Target(
        library="openinference", code_path="openai-agents",
        packages=(

"""The model drafts the smallest change plus a unit test; code checks and applies it to the clone.

The draft is JSON: exact search/replace edits on files of the target's packages,
and one new test file in the package's tests directory. Code refuses edits outside
those packages, an `old` text that is not found exactly once, and a test file
outside the tests directory. Whether the patch is kept is decided by verify.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from trueup.fixer.targets import Target

SYSTEM = """You fix bugs in AI tracing libraries (OpenTelemetry instrumentations). Trueup ran a real agent \
against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened, and found that the library's spans disagree with it. \
You get the finding, the located wrapper code and its callers, and how the right behaviour looks.

Draft the SMALLEST change that makes the spans match what happened, in the library's own style, plus ONE new \
unit test written like the package's existing tests (same fixtures, same imports, no network, no API keys, no \
cassettes) that fails on the current code and passes with your change. Do not change existing tests. Do not \
reformat code you do not change.

Reply with JSON only:
{"explanation": "cause and fix in 2-4 plain sentences",
 "edits": [{"file": "<path from the repo root>", "old": "<exact text in the file, unique, with enough context>", \
"new": "<replacement>"}],
 "test": {"file": "<path from the repo root, in the package's tests dir, new file named test_trueup_*.py>", \
"content": "<the whole test file>"}}"""


class PatchError(ValueError):
    """The draft cannot be applied. The reason goes back to the model."""


def test_style(clone: Path, target: Target, limit: int = 14_000) -> str:
    """conftest.py and the shortest test files of the first package, to show its test style."""
    tests = clone / target.packages[0].path / target.packages[0].tests
    parts, total = [], 0
    files = [tests / "conftest.py"] + sorted((f for f in tests.glob("test_*.py")), key=lambda f: f.stat().st_size)
    for f in files:
        if not f.exists():
            continue
        text = f.read_text(errors="replace")[:8000]
        if total + len(text) > limit:
            break
        total += len(text)
        parts.append(f"### {f.relative_to(clone)}\n{text}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def first_prompt(finding: dict[str, Any], target: Target, located: dict[str, Any], source: str,
                 style: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    d = finding["details"]
    leads = [{k: x.get(k) for k in ("scenario", "field", "truth", "trace")} for x in d.get("leads", [])]
    user = (f"Library: {target.library} (repo commit {located['commit'][:10]}).\n"
            f"Finding {finding['id']}: {finding['title']} (severity {finding['severity']}).\n"
            f"Check: {d['check']}; field: {d['field']}.\nTruth vs trace per scenario:\n{json.dumps(leads)}\n"
            f"Scenarios: {', '.join(d['scenarios'])}. Scenarios of this code path that are right today must stay "
            f"right.\nRight behaviour: {target.reference_note}\nChecker's reference rule: "
            f"{d.get('rules', {}).get('reference', '')}\n\n"
            f"Packages you may change: {', '.join(p.path for p in target.packages)}.\n"
            f"Located definitions:\n{json.dumps(located['definitions'])}\n"
            f"Callers:\n{json.dumps(located['callers'][:60])}\n\n"
            f"Source:\n{source}\n\nTest style of {target.packages[0].path}:\n{style}")
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def revision_prompt(messages: list[dict[str, str]], draft: Any, reason: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    return [*messages, {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps(draft)},
            {"role": "user", "content": "That patch was rejected:\n" + reason +
             "\n\nRevise it. Reply with the whole JSON again (edits against the ORIGINAL files, the full test "
             "file)."}]


def check_draft(draft: Any, clone: Path, target: Target) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """The edits plus the test as file writes. Raises PatchError with the reason."""
    if not isinstance(draft, dict) or not isinstance(draft.get("edits"), list) or not draft["edits"]:
        raise PatchError('the reply needs a non-empty "edits" list')
    test = draft.get("test")
    if not isinstance(test, dict) or not test.get("file") or not test.get("content"):
        raise PatchError('the reply needs "test": {"file", "content"}')
    allowed = [p.path.strip("./") for p in target.packages]
    allowed = [a + "/" if a else "" for a in allowed]

    def inside(path: str) -> bool:
        return not Path(path).is_absolute() and ".." not in Path(path).parts and any(
            path.startswith(a) for a in allowed)

    files: dict[str, str] = {}
    for e in draft["edits"]:
        if not isinstance(e, dict) or not all(isinstance(e.get(k), str) for k in ("file", "old", "new")):
            raise PatchError('each edit needs string "file", "old" and "new"')
        f = e["file"]
        if not inside(f) or "/tests/" in f"/{f}":
            raise PatchError(f"edit to {f} is outside the library code you may change ({', '.join(allowed)})")
        path = clone / f
        if not path.exists():
            raise PatchError(f"{f} does not exist")
        text = files.get(f, path.read_text())
        n = text.count(e["old"])
        if n != 1:
            raise PatchError(f"the old text of an edit to {f} is found {n} times, not once: "
                             f"{e['old'][:120]!r}")
        files[f] = text.replace(e["old"], e["new"], 1)
    tf = test["file"]
    pkg = next((p for p in target.packages if tf.startswith((p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path.strip("./") else "")
                                                              + p.tests + "/")), None)
    if pkg is None or not inside(tf) or not Path(tf).name.startswith("test_trueup_") or not tf.endswith(".py"):
        raise PatchError(f"the test file {tf} must be a new test_trueup_*.py in a package's tests dir")
    if (clone / tf).exists():
        raise PatchError(f"the test file {tf} already exists")
    for f, text in files.items():
        try:
            compile(text, f, "exec")
        except SyntaxError as e:
            raise PatchError(f"{f} does not compile after the edits: {e.msg} at line {e.lineno}") from None
    try:
        compile(test["content"], tf, "exec")
    except SyntaxError as e:
        raise PatchError(f"the test file does not compile: {e.msg} at line {e.lineno}") from None
    return [{"file": f, "content": t} for f, t in files.items()]


def write_files(clone: Path, writes: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    for w in writes:
        p = clone / w["file"]
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(w["content"])


def diff(clone: Path) -> str:
    """git diff of the clone, new files included."""
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "add", "-N", "."], capture_output=True, timeout=60)
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "diff"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    return p.stdout

"""trueup fix <finding-id>: locate the wrapper, let the model draft a patch and a test, and verify it.

Steps, one library at a time:
  1. locate (trueup.fixer.locate): shallow clone in .trueup/clones/<lib>; Entire's code graph if it
     is there, else ripgrep + ast; locate.json in the run dir and in fixes/<id>/
  2. baseline (verifier): the target packages' own test suites on the clean clone, and the full
     scenario library in .trueup/venvs/<lib>-fix built from the clean clone
  3. up to MAX_TRIES tries: the model drafts edits + a test (trueup.fixer.patch); code applies them;
     the verifier checks that the new test fails before and passes after, the suites show no new
     failure, the finding's scenarios now match truth, and the full library shows no new mismatch.
     A failed try goes back to the model with the reason.
Writes fixes/<id>/: patch.diff, the test file, before-after.md/json, suites.json, locate.json,
tries.json and summary.md. Nothing is committed, pushed or posted. The clone is reset at the end.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.fixer import locate as loc
from trueup.fixer import patch as pt
from trueup.fixer import targets as tg
from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup.model import PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, record_spend

MAX_TRIES = 3


def find_finding(root: Path, finding_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]:
    """The finding with this id in the newest findings.json that has it."""
    for f in sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob("*/findings.json"), reverse=True):
        for x in json.loads(f.read_text())["findings"]:
            if x["id"] == finding_id:
                return x, f.parent
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no finding {finding_id!r} in .trueup/runs/*/findings.json")


def all_scenarios() -> list[str]:
    from trueup.scenarios import select
    from trueup.scenarios.proposed import load

    return [s.id for s in select("all")] + [s.id for s in load()]


def _touched(target: tg.Target, files: list[str]) -> list[tg.Package]:
    return [p for p in target.packages if any(f.startswith(p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path != "." else "")
                                              for f in files)]


def _short(s: str, n: int = 600) -> str:
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[: n - 3] + "..."


def baseline(root: Path, clone: Path, commit: str, target: tg.Target, fix_dir: Path,
             out: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Suites and sweep on the clean clone. Cached in fix_dir per commit."""
    cache = fix_dir / "baseline.json"
    if cache.exists():
        b = json.loads(cache.read_text())
        if b.get("commit") == commit:
            out("baseline: cached for this commit")
            return b
    out("baseline: building the test venv")
    tpy = vf.ensure_test_venv(root, clone, target)
    suites = {}
    for p in target.packages:
        out(f"baseline: {p.path} test suite (clean clone)")
        suites[p.path] = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, p, [p.tests])
        s = suites[p.path]
        out(f"  {s.get('passed', '?')} passed, {s.get('failed', '?')} failed, {s.get('errors', '?')} errors, "
            f"exit {s['exit']}")
    out("baseline: building the scenario venv from the clean clone")
    fpy = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library)
    vf.reinstall(fpy, clone, target)
    out("baseline: full scenario library")
    sweep = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, all_scenarios(), out=out)
    b = {"commit": commit, "suites": suites, "sweep": sweep}
    cache.write_text(json.dumps(b, indent=1, default=str))
    return b


def verify_try(root: Path, clone: Path, target: tg.Target, finding: dict[str, Any], draft: dict[str, Any],
               writes: list[dict[str, str]], base: dict[str, Any], out: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Apply the try to the clean clone step by step. Returns the try's record with ok and reason."""
    rec: dict[str, Any] = {"ok": False}
    test = draft["test"]
    pkg_of_test = next(p for p in target.packages if test["file"].startswith(
        (p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path != "." else "") + p.tests + "/"))
    test_rel = str(Path(test["file"]).relative_to(pkg_of_test.path)) if pkg_of_test.path != "." else test["file"]
    tpy = vf.ensure_test_venv(root, clone, target)
    loc.reset_clone(clone)
    pt.write_files(clone, [{"file": test["file"], "content": test["content"]}])
    out("  new test on the unpatched code")
    t_before = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, pkg_of_test, [test_rel])
    pt.write_files(clone, writes)
    out("  new test on the patched code")
    t_after = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, pkg_of_test, [test_rel])
    ok, why = vf.new_test_verdict(t_before, t_after)
    rec["new_test"] = {"before": t_before, "after": t_after, "ok": ok, "reason": why}
    out(f"  {why[:300]}")
    if not ok:
        rec["reason"] = why
        return rec
    rec["suites"] = {}
    for p in _touched(target, [w["file"] for w in writes] + [test["file"]]):
        out(f"  {p.path} test suite (patched)")
        after = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, p, [p.tests])
        ok, why = vf.suite_verdict(base["suites"][p.path], after, test["file"])
        rec["suites"][p.path] = {"after": after, "ok": ok, "reason": why}
        out(f"  {why[:300]}")
        if not ok:
            rec["reason"] = f"{p.path}: {why}"
            return rec
    fpy = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library) if False else \
        vf.venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{target.library}-fix") / "bin" / "python"
    vf.reinstall(fpy, clone, target)
    out("  the finding's scenarios (patched)")
    scen = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, finding["details"]["scenarios"], out=out)
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(scen, finding)
    rec["scenarios"] = {"ok": ok, "reason": why}
    out(f"  {why}")
    if not ok:
        rec["reason"] = why
        return rec
    out("  full scenario library (patched)")
    full = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, all_scenarios(), out=out)
    new = vf.new_mismatches(base["sweep"], full)
    rec["sweep"] = {"totals": vf.totals(full), "new_mismatches": new}
    rec["sweep_after"] = full
    if new:
        rec["reason"] = (f"{len(new)} new mismatch(es) in the full scenario library: " +
                         "; ".join(f"{m['scenario']} {m['check']} {m['field']}: truth {m['truth']}, trace "
                                   f"{m['trace']}" for m in new[:8]))
        out(f"  {rec['reason'][:300]}")
        return rec
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(full, finding)
    rec.update(ok=ok, reason=why if ok else f"full sweep: {why}")
    return rec


def fix(root: Path, finding_id: str, *, client: ModelClient | None = None, run_id: str | None = None,
        out: Callable[[str], None] = print, max_tries: int = MAX_TRIES) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from trueup.sweep import new_run_id

    finding, found_in = find_finding(root, finding_id)
    target = tg.get(finding["library"], finding["details"]["code_path"])
    run_id = run_id or new_run_id(f"fix-{finding['library']}")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    fix_dir = root / "fixes" / finding_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fix_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = client or ModelClient()
    record_spend(run_dir, "before", client)
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"finding": finding_id, "title": finding["title"], "library": target.library,
                              "found_in": found_in.name, "run_id": run_id, "session_id": tracing.session_id(),
                              "model": PLAN_MODEL, "started": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
                              "tries": [], "fixed": False, "error": None}
    clone = None
    try:
        with tracing.worker("trueup-fixer", step="locate") as span:
            located = loc.locate(root, target, run_dir)
            clone = Path(located["clone"])
            loc.reset_clone(clone)
            (fix_dir / "locate.json").write_text((run_dir / "locate.json").read_text())
            result["commit"], result["locate_method"] = located["commit"], located["method"]
            out(f"located with {located['method']}: {len(located['definitions'])} definitions, "
                f"{len(located['callers'])} callers ({located['graph'].get('reason', '')[:160]})")
            tracing.set_verdict(span, located["method"])
        with tracing.worker("trueup-verifier", step="baseline") as span:
            base = baseline(root, clone, located["commit"], target, fix_dir, out)
            tracing.set_verdict(span, f"baseline: {vf.totals(base['sweep'])['leads']} leads")
        result["suites_before"] = {k: {x: v.get(x) for x in ("total", "passed", "failed", "errors", "skipped",
                                                              "failing", "exit")} for k, v in base["suites"].items()}
        messages = pt.first_prompt(finding, target, located, loc.source_excerpts(clone, located),
                                   pt.test_style(clone, target))
        for n in range(1, max_tries + 1):
            out(f"try {n}/{max_tries}: asking {PLAN_MODEL} for a patch")
            rec: dict[str, Any] = {"try": n}
            with tracing.worker("trueup-fixer", step=f"draft {n}") as span:
                draft = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, messages, max_tokens=12000)
                rec["explanation"] = draft.get("explanation") if isinstance(draft, dict) else None
                rec["draft"] = draft
                try:
                    writes = pt.check_draft(draft, clone, target)
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "applies")
                except pt.PatchError as e:
                    rec.update(ok=False, stage="apply", reason=f"patch does not apply: {e}")
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "does not apply")
            if "stage" not in rec:
                with tracing.worker("trueup-verifier", step=f"try {n}") as span:
                    rec.update(verify_try(root, clone, target, finding, draft, writes, base, out))
                    rec["stage"] = "verified" if rec["ok"] else "verify"
                    rec["diff"] = pt.diff(clone)
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "pass" if rec["ok"] else "fail")
            out(f"try {n}: {'PASS' if rec['ok'] else 'FAIL'}: {_short(rec['reason'], 400)}")
            result["tries"].append(rec)
            if rec["ok"]:
                result["fixed"] = True
                write_fix(fix_dir, finding, target, base, rec)
                break
            messages = pt.revision_prompt(messages, draft, rec["reason"])
    except (ModelError, vf.VerifyError, RuntimeError) as e:
        result["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        out(f"fixer stopped: {result['error']}")
    finally:
        if clone is not None:
            loc.reset_clone(clone)
        record_spend(run_dir, "after", client)
        spend = json.loads((run_dir / "spend.json").read_text())
        result["usage"], result["cost_usd"] = spend.get("usage"), spend.get("run_cost_usd")
        result["spend_after_usd"] = spend.get("after", {}).get("spend_usd")
        write_log(fix_dir, run_dir, result)
    out(f"{finding_id}: {'fixed, verified' if result['fixed'] else 'NOT fixed'} after {len(result['tries'])} "
        f"tr{'y' if len(result['tries']) == 1 else 'ies'}; model cost ${result['cost_usd']}; wrote {fix_dir}")
    return result


def write_fix(fix_dir: Path, finding: dict[str, Any], target: tg.Target, base: dict[str, Any],
              rec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    (fix_dir / "patch.diff").write_text(rec["diff"])
    test = rec["draft"]["test"]
    (fix_dir / Path(test["file"]).name).write_text(test["content"])
    rows = vf.before_after(finding, base["sweep"], rec["sweep_after"])
    tb, ta = vf.totals(base["sweep"]), vf.totals(rec["sweep_after"])
    (fix_dir / "before-after.json").write_text(json.dumps({"rows": rows, "before": tb, "after": ta}, indent=1,
                                                          default=str))
    (fix_dir / "before-after.md").write_text(vf.table_md(rows, tb, ta))


def write_log(fix_dir: Path, run_dir: Path, result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    tries = []
    for t in result["tries"]:
        t = {k: v for k, v in t.items() if k != "sweep_after"}
        tries.append(t)
    log = {**result, "tries": tries}
    (fix_dir / "tries.json").write_text(json.dumps(log, indent=1, default=str))
    (run_dir / "fix.json").write_text(json.dumps(log, indent=1, default=str))
    suites = {"before": result.get("suites_before", {}),
              "after": {n: {p: {x: s["after"].get(x) for x in ("total", "passed", "failed", "errors", "skipped",
                                                                  "failing", "exit")} | {"verdict": s["reason"]}
                            for p, s in t.get("suites", {}).items()} for n, t in
                        ((t["try"], t) for t in result["tries"])}}
    (fix_dir / "suites.json").write_text(json.dumps(suites, indent=1, default=str))
    lines = [f"# {result['finding']}", "", result["title"], "",
             f"Library commit: {result.get('commit', '?')}. Located with {result.get('locate_method', '?')}.",
             f"Model: {result['model']}; cost ${result['cost_usd']} (key spend delta); run {result['run_id']}.", "",
             "Result: " + ("fixed: the new test fails before and passes after, the suites show no new failure, the "
                           "finding's scenarios match truth and the full scenario library has no new mismatch."
                           if result["fixed"] else "NOT fixed. No patch is offered."
                           + (f" Stopped: {result['error']}" if result["error"] else "")), "", "## Tries", ""]
    for t in result["tries"]:
        lines.append(f"{t['try']}. {'PASS' if t['ok'] else 'FAIL'} at {t.get('stage')}: {_short(t['reason'], 700)}")
        if t.get("explanation"):
            lines.append(f"   Model's explanation: {_short(t['explanation'], 500)}")
    if (fix_dir / "before-after.md").exists() and result["fixed"]:
        lines += ["", "## Before and after", "", (fix_dir / "before-after.md").read_text()]
    (fix_dir / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

new='''def find_finding(root: Path, finding_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]:
    """The finding with this id, from the newest findings.json that has it. The id names the library,

    planner proposals) is the same finding: their scenarios and leads are added to it."""
    found: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]] = []

    finding, run_dir = json.loads(json.dumps(found[0][0])), found[0][1]

"""trueup upstream <finding-id>: draft issue and PR text into upstream/<finding-id>/. Never posts.

The text is built from recorded data: the finding, the fix's before/after table and suite results
(fixes/<id>/), the scenarios on the same code path that are right (the boundary), and a standalone
repro that needs only the library and the provider SDK (httpx.MockTransport answers; no keys, no
network). The repro is run here, on the latest release and on the clone with patch.diff applied,
and its output goes into the text. The issue follows the repo's issue template when it has one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import platform
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from trueup.core.repro import line_count
from trueup.fix import find_finding
from trueup.fixer import locate as loc
from trueup.fixer import targets as tg
from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup.runner import venvs
from trueup.runner.setups import VERSIONED

MAX_REPRO_LINES = 40

_AGENTS_BODY = '''BODY = {"id": "resp_1", "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "status": "completed", "model": "m",
        "output": [{"type": "message", "id": "msg_1", "role": "assistant", "status": "completed",
                    "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Hello!", "annotations": []}]}],
        "parallel_tool_calls": True, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [],
        "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 18,
                  "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}}}'''

REPROS: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {
    ("openllmetry", "openai-agents"): '''"""OpenLLMetry + OpenAI Agents SDK: one model call is recorded as two LLM spans.
Needs traceloop-sdk and openai-agents. Offline: httpx.MockTransport answers. Leave OPENAI_API_KEY
unset so the Agents SDK's own exporter skips its upload."""
import asyncio

import httpx
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
from traceloop.sdk import Traceloop

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
Traceloop.init(app_name="repro", exporter=exporter, disable_batch=True, telemetry_enabled=False)
from agents import Agent, OpenAIResponsesModel, Runner  # noqa: E402

''' + _AGENTS_BODY + '''
transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(200, json=BODY))
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake/v1", http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport))
agent = Agent(name="helper", model=OpenAIResponsesModel("m", client))
asyncio.run(Runner.run(agent, "hi"))
llm = [s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.attributes.get("gen_ai.operation.name") == "chat"]
tokens = sum(s.attributes.get("gen_ai.usage.output_tokens", 0) for s in llm)
print(f"provider requests: 1; LLM spans: {len(llm)}; output tokens on LLM spans: {tokens} (provider sent 7)")
''',
    ("openinference", "openai-agents"): '''"""OpenInference + OpenAI Agents SDK: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK.
Needs openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents and openai-agents. Offline: httpx.MockTransport
answers HTTP 500. Leave OPENAI_API_KEY unset so the Agents SDK's own exporter skips its upload."""
import asyncio

import httpx
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from openinference.instrumentation.openai_agents import OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
from agents import Agent, OpenAIResponsesModel, Runner  # noqa: E402

transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(500, json={"error": {"message": "boom"}}))
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake/v1", max_retries=0,
                     http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport))
agent = Agent(name="helper", model=OpenAIResponsesModel("m", client))
try:
    asyncio.run(Runner.run(agent, "hi"))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"the run raised {type(e).__name__}")
root = next(s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.parent is None)
print(f"top-level span {root.name!r}: {root.status.status_code.name}")
''',
    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): '''"""neatlogs + Anthropic messages.stream(): a stream that fails leaves the span OK.
Needs neatlogs and anthropic. Offline: httpx.MockTransport answers with an SSE stream that ends in an
error event; export is off."""
import json

import anthropic
import httpx
import neatlogs
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter, provider = InMemorySpanExporter(), TracerProvider()
neatlogs.init(api_key="x", instrumentations=["anthropic"], disable_export=True, tracer_provider=provider)
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
start = {"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": "msg_1", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": "m",
         "content": [], "stop_reason": None, "usage": {"input_tokens": 5, "output_tokens": 0}}}
error = {"type": "error", "error": {"type": "overloaded_error", "message": "Overloaded"}}
sse = "".join(f"event: {e['type']}\\ndata: {json.dumps(e)}\\n\\n" for e in (start, error))
transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda r: httpx.Response(200, text=sse, headers={"content-type": "text/event-stream"}))
client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake", http_client=httpx.Client(transport=transport))
try:
    with client.messages.stream(model="m", max_tokens=16, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]) as s:
        "".join(s.text_stream)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"the app saw {type(e).__name__}")
neatlogs.flush()
for span in exporter.get_finished_spans():
    print(f"span {span.name!r}: {span.status.status_code.name}, exception events: "
          f"{sum(e.name == 'exception' for e in span.events)}")
''',
}

# Per library: the template's component, the PR title prefix and the issue template file.
META = {
    ("openllmetry", "openai-agents"): {
        "component": "OpenAI Instrumentation", "pr_title": "fix(openai-agents): record one LLM span per model call",
        "title": "OpenAI Agents SDK: every non-streamed model call is recorded as two LLM spans (calls and tokens "
                 "doubled)"},
    ("openinference", "openai-agents"): {
        "pr_title": "fix(openai-agents): set the root span to ERROR when the agent run fails",
        "title": "openai-agents: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK"},
    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): {
        "pr_title": "fix(anthropic): record an error on messages.stream() spans when the stream fails",
        "title": "Anthropic messages.stream(): a stream that fails (error event or cut connection) is recorded as OK"},
}


def run_repro(py: Path, script: str, timeout: float = 180) -> dict[str, Any]:
    env = vf.test_env()
    env.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)  # the Agents SDK's own exporter then skips its upload
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-upstream-") as tmp:
        f = Path(tmp) / "repro.py"
        f.write_text(script)
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([str(py), str(f)], cwd=tmp, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {"exit": -1, "stdout": "", "stderr": f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s"}
    return {"exit": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout.strip(), "stderr": p.stderr.strip()[-1500:]}


def versions(py: Path, library: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    code = ("import json, importlib.metadata as m\nout = {}\nfor d in " + json.dumps(VERSIONED[library]) +
            ":\n    try: out[d] = m.version(d)\n    except Exception: pass\nprint(json.dumps(out))")
    p = subprocess.run([str(py), "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    return json.loads(p.stdout) if p.returncode == 0 else {}


def boundary(finding: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Scenarios on the same code path (id prefix) that are right before the patch, from the fix's baseline."""
    base = json.loads((fix_dir / "baseline.json").read_text())["sweep"] if (fix_dir / "baseline.json").exists() \
        else {"leads": {}}
    d = finding["details"]
    prefixes = tuple({sid.split("-", 1)[0] + "-" for sid in d["scenarios"]})
    same = [sid for sid in base["leads"] if sid.startswith(prefixes)]
    right = [sid for sid in same if sid not in d["scenarios"] and not any(
        vf.matches_finding(m, finding) for m in base["leads"][sid])]
    return {"affected": d["scenarios"], "right": right}


def patched_python(root: Path, target: tg.Target, fix_dir: Path) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:
    """The -fix venv with patch.diff applied to the clean clone and installed. (None, reason) if no fix."""
    diff = fix_dir / "patch.diff"
    if not diff.exists():
        return None, "no verified fix in fixes/ for this finding"
    clone, _ = loc.ensure_clone(root, target.library)
    loc.reset_clone(clone)
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "apply", str(diff.resolve())], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        loc.reset_clone(clone)
        return None, f"patch.diff does not apply to the clone: {p.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
    try:
        py = venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{target.library}-fix") / "bin" / "python"
        if not py.exists():
            py = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library)
        vf.reinstall(py, clone, target)
    finally:
        loc.reset_clone(clone)
    return py, "patched"


def upstream(root: Path, finding_id: str, out: Any = print) -> Path:
    finding, _ = find_finding(root, finding_id)
    key = (finding["library"], finding["details"]["code_path"])
    target = tg.get(*key)
    script = REPROS[key]
    n = line_count(script)
    if n >= MAX_REPRO_LINES:
        raise ValueError(f"the repro has {n} lines; it must be under {MAX_REPRO_LINES}")
    fix_dir = root / "fixes" / finding_id
    up_dir = root / "upstream" / finding_id
    up_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fix = json.loads((fix_dir / "tries.json").read_text()) if (fix_dir / "tries.json").exists() else None
    out("running the repro on the latest release")
    before_py = venvs.ensure(root, target.library)
    before = run_repro(before_py, script)
    after_py, why = patched_python(root, target, fix_dir) if fix and fix.get("fixed") else (None, "no verified fix")
    out(f"running the repro on the patched clone ({why})")
    after = run_repro(after_py, script) if after_py else None
    env = {"python": platform.python_version(), "os": f"{platform.system()} {platform.machine()}",
           "latest release": versions(before_py, target.library),
           "patched": {"commit": fix.get("commit") if fix else None, "packages": [p.path for p in target.packages]}}
    data = {"finding": finding_id, "repro_lines": n, "before": before, "after": after, "after_note": why,
            "environment": env, "boundary": boundary(finding, fix_dir), "fixed": bool(fix and fix.get("fixed")),
            "posted": False}
    (up_dir / "repro.py").write_text(script)
    (up_dir / "repro-output.json").write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1))
    (up_dir / "issue.md").write_text(issue_text(root, finding, target, data, fix_dir))
    (up_dir / "pr.md").write_text(pr_text(finding, target, data, fix_dir, fix))
    out(f"repro ({n} lines) before: {before['stdout'] or before['stderr'][-200:]}")
    if after:
        out(f"repro after the patch: {after['stdout'] or after['stderr'][-200:]}")
    out(f"wrote {up_dir} (nothing posted)")
    return up_dir


def _code(text: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    return f"```{lang}\n{text.rstrip()}\n```"


def _sections(finding: dict[str, Any], target: tg.Target, data: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    d = finding["details"]
    b = data["boundary"]
    table = (fix_dir / "before-after.md").read_text() if (fix_dir / "before-after.md").exists() else ""
    rows = "\n".join(f"- `{x['scenario']}`: {x['field']} should be {x['truth']}, the trace has {x['trace']}"
                     for x in d.get("leads", []))
    return {
        "symptom": (f"{META[(target.library, target.code_path)]['title']}.\n\nTrueup ran each case against a fake "
                    f"provider, so it knows what really happened, and compared that with the exported spans:\n\n"
                    f"{rows}"),
        "boundary": (f"Affected: {', '.join(f'`{s}`' for s in b['affected'])}.\n\nRight today on the same code "
                     f"path: {', '.join(f'`{s}`' for s in b['right']) or 'none'}.\n\nReproduces on the latest "
                     f"release and on main ({d.get('rules', {}).get('latest_and_main', '')})."),
        "repro": (f"Standalone, {data['repro_lines']} lines, needs only the library and the SDK; no API key, no "
                  f"network:\n\n{_code(REPROS[(target.library, target.code_path)], 'python')}\n\nOutput on the "
                  f"latest release:\n\n{_code(data['before']['stdout'] or data['before']['stderr'])}"),
        "expected": target.reference_note,
        "table": table,
        "environment": (f"Python {data['environment']['python']}, {data['environment']['os']}. Versions: " +
                        ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in data["environment"]["latest release"].items()) + "."),
        "dedupe": "; ".join(f"`{s['query']}` ({s['hits']} hits, {s['date'][:10]})"
                            for s in finding.get("dedupe", {}).get("searches", [])),
    }


def issue_text(root: Path, finding: dict[str, Any], target: tg.Target, data: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path) -> str:
    s = _sections(finding, target, data, fix_dir)
    meta = META[(target.library, target.code_path)]
    note = "<!-- Drafted by Trueup from recorded runs. Not posted. -->\n\n"
    if target.library == "openllmetry":  # .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
        return note + "\n\n".join([
            f"# 🐛 Bug Report: {meta['title']}",
            f"### Which component is this bug for?\n\n{meta['component']} (the fix is in "
            "opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents and opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai)",
            f"### 📜 Description\n\n{s['symptom']}\n\n{s['boundary']}",
            f"### 👟 Reproduction steps\n\n{s['repro']}",
            f"### 👍 Expected behavior\n\n{s['expected']}",
            f"### 👎 Actual Behavior with Screenshots\n\n{s['table'] or 'See the repro output.'}",
            f"### 🤖 Python Version\n\n{data['environment']['python']}",
            f"### 📃 Provide any additional context for the Bug.\n\n{s['environment']}",
            f"### 👀 Have you spent some time to check if this bug has been raised before?\n\n- [x] I checked and "
            f"didn't find similar issue (searched issues and PRs in all states: {s['dedupe']})",
            "### Are you willing to submit PR?\n\nYes I am willing to submit a PR!"])
    if target.library == "openinference":  # .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md
        return note + "\n\n".join([
            f"# [bug] {meta['title']}",
            f"**Describe the bug**\n\n{s['symptom']}\n\n{s['boundary']}",
            f"**To Reproduce**\n\n{s['repro']}",
            f"**Expected behavior**\n\n{s['expected']}",
            "**Screenshots**\n\nNone; the repro prints the span status.",
            f"**Environment**\n\n{s['environment']}",
            f"**Additional context**\n\nBefore and after the proposed fix, from Trueup's runs:\n\n{s['table']}\n"
            f"Searched issues and PRs first: {s['dedupe']}."])
    return note + "\n\n".join([  # neatlogs has no issue template
        f"# {meta['title']}", f"## Symptom\n\n{s['symptom']}", f"## Boundary\n\n{s['boundary']}",
        f"## Repro\n\n{s['repro']}", f"## Expected\n\n{s['expected']}",
        f"## Before and after the proposed fix\n\n{s['table']}", f"## Environment\n\n{s['environment']}",
        f"Searched issues and PRs first: {s['dedupe']}."])


def pr_text(finding: dict[str, Any], target: tg.Target, data: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path,
            fix: dict[str, Any] | None) -> str:
    meta = META[(target.library, target.code_path)]
    head = "<!-- Drafted by Trueup from recorded runs. Not posted. -->\n\n"
    if not data["fixed"] or not fix:
        return head + f"# {meta['pr_title']}\n\nNo verified fix: {data['after_note']}. No PR is proposed.\n"
    ok = next(t for t in fix["tries"] if t["ok"])
    s = _sections(finding, target, data, fix_dir)
    suites = "\n".join(f"- `{p}`: {v['reason']}" for p, v in ok.get("suites", {}).items())
    before = "\n".join(f"- `{p}` before the patch: {v['passed']} passed, {len(v['failing'])} failing"
                       + (f" ({', '.join(t.rsplit('::', 1)[-1] for t in v['failing'])})" if v["failing"] else "")
                       for p, v in fix.get("suites_before", {}).items())
    files = sorted({ln[6:] for ln in (fix_dir / "patch.diff").read_text().splitlines() if ln.startswith("+++ b/")})
    after = data["after"]["stdout"] if data["after"] else "(not run)"
    body = [f"# {meta['pr_title']}", f"## What\n\n{ok.get('explanation') or ''}",
            "## Files\n\n" + "\n".join(f"- `{f}`" for f in files),
            f"## Test\n\n{ok['new_test']['reason']}.", f"## Suites\n\n{before}\n{suites}",
            f"## Before and after\n\n{s['table']}\nThe standalone repro from the issue, with this patch:\n\n"
            f"{_code(after)}"]
    if target.library == "openllmetry":  # .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
        body.append("- [x] I have added tests that cover my changes.\n- [ ] If adding a new instrumentation or "
                    "changing an existing one, I've added screenshots from some observability platform showing the "
                    "change. (Not done: the change was checked with in-memory spans, see the table.)\n- [x] PR name "
                    "follows conventional commits format: `feat(instrumentation): ...` or `fix(instrumentation): "
                    "...`.\n- [ ] (If applicable) I have updated the documentation accordingly. (Not applicable.)")
    body.append(f"Patch drafted by {fix['model']} and verified by Trueup ({len(fix['tries'])} tries in the last run; "
                "every try is in tries.json).")
    return head + "\n\n".join(body) + "\n"

# [bug] openai-agents: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK

**Describe the bug**

openai-agents: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK.

Trueup ran each case against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened, and compared that with the exported spans:

- `ag-llm-fails`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised InternalServerError), the trace has OK
- `ag-max-turns`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised MaxTurnsExceeded), the trace has OK
- `ag-bad-tool`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised ModelBehaviorError), the trace has OK
- `ag-streamed-error`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised ModelBehaviorError), the trace has OK
- `ag-streamed-cut`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised APIConnectionError), the trace has OK

Affected: `ag-bad-tool`, `ag-llm-fails`, `ag-max-turns`, `ag-streamed-cut`, `ag-streamed-error`.

Right today on the same code path: `ag-run`, `ag-tool-raises`, `ag-streamed`.

Reproduces on the latest release and on main (latest release and main c364180e5b).

**To Reproduce**

Standalone, 28 lines, needs only the library and the SDK; no API key, no network:

```python
"""OpenInference + OpenAI Agents SDK: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK.
Needs openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents and openai-agents. Offline: httpx.MockTransport
answers HTTP 500. Leave OPENAI_API_KEY unset so the Agents SDK's own exporter skips its upload."""
import asyncio

import httpx
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from openinference.instrumentation.openai_agents import OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
from agents import Agent, OpenAIResponsesModel, Runner  # noqa: E402

transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(500, json={"error": {"message": "boom"}}))
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake/v1", max_retries=0,
                     http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport))
agent = Agent(name="helper", model=OpenAIResponsesModel("m", client))
try:
    asyncio.run(Runner.run(agent, "hi"))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"the run raised {type(e).__name__}")
root = next(s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.parent is None)
print(f"top-level span {root.name!r}: {root.status.status_code.name}")
```

Output on the latest release:

```
the run raised InternalServerError
top-level span 'Agent workflow': OK
```

**Expected behavior**

OTel conventions: a span whose operation failed has status ERROR. The root span covers the whole run, so it must not be OK when the run raised. Which SDK span carries the error differs by failure (the agent span, a turn span or a response span; see the spans below). A run whose tool raised but which still finished must stay OK: the SDK marks that function span with a non-fatal error.

None; the repro prints the span status.

from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup import upstream as up

TARGET = tg.Target(library="lib", code_path="x", packages=(tg.Package("pkg", "pkg"),), seeds=("wrap",),
                   reference_seeds=("KEY",))


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    (tmp_path / "pkg" / "lib").mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp_path / "pkg" / "tests").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "pkg" / "lib" / "w.py").write_text(
        "KEY = 1\n\n\nclass P:\n    def wrap(self, x):\n        return x\n\n    def use(self):\n"
        "        return self.wrap(1)\n\n\ndef top():\n    return P().wrap(2)\n")
    (tmp_path / "build" / "lib").mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp_path / "build" / "lib" / "w.py").write_text("def wrap():\n    pass\n")
    return tmp_path


def draft(**kw):
    d = {"edits": [{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "        return x\n", "new": "        return x + 1\n"}],
         "test": {"file": "pkg/tests/test_trueup_w.py", "content": "def test_x():\n    assert True\n"}}
    d.update(kw)
    return d


def test_check_draft_applies_and_returns_writes(repo: Path) -> None:
    writes = pt.check_draft(draft(), repo, TARGET)
    assert writes == [{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "content": (repo / "pkg/lib/w.py").read_text().replace(
        "return x\n", "return x + 1\n")}]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("edits, reason", [
    ([{"file": "other/w.py", "old": "a", "new": "b"}], "outside"),
    ([{"file": "build/lib/w.py", "old": "pass", "new": "x"}], "outside"),
    ([{"file": "pkg/tests/test_a.py", "old": "a", "new": "b"}], "outside"),
    ([{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "    return x\n", "new": ""}], "found 0 times"),  # indentation differs
    ([{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "wrap(", "new": "w("}], "found 3 times"),
    ([{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "        return x\n", "new": "        return (\n"}], "does not compile"),
    ([], "non-empty"),
])

                       repo, TARGET)

content.text:
I built `trueup fix` and `trueup upstream` and ran them on all three findings, including the optional neatlogs one. All three now have a verified fix and drafted upstream text. `uv run pytest -q` passes (298 tests). Nothing was committed, pushed or posted.

**What the commands do**
- **`trueup fix <finding-id>`** finds the code behind a finding in a shallow clone (`.trueup/clones/<lib>`). The model then drafts the smallest change plus one new test, and code applies it to the clone. A try is kept only if all of these hold:
  - the new test fails before the patch and passes after;
  - the package's own test suite shows no new failure, the new test included;
  - the finding's scenarios now match truth;
  - all 57 scenarios, run against the patched package, show no new mismatch.
- A failed try goes back to the model with the reason, at most 3 tries per run. Everything is written to `fixes/<id>/`, and each run's tries are kept in `runs/`. Both workers are traced in neatlogs as `trueup-fixer` and `trueup-verifier`.
- **`trueup upstream <finding-id>`** writes `issue.md` and `pr.md` into `upstream/<id>/`, following each repo's templates (neatlogs has none). Each includes a standalone repro of 27–30 lines that needs only the library and the SDK. The repro is run on the latest release and on the patched clone, and both outputs go into the text.

**Entire's code graph was not used.** `entire agent-help` lists no graph command, and `entire graph` says the plugin isn't installed. `agent-help` marks `entire plugin` as yours to run, so I didn't install it. The fixer fell back to ripgrep plus Python's ast, and every `locate.json` records the Entire output and this reason.

**Results**

| finding | runs (tries) | before → after | suite after the patch |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenLLMetry: double LLM spans | 5 runs, passed on try 3 of the last | ag-run 4 spans → 2 (truth 2); repro 2 spans / 14 tokens → 1 / 7 | 409 passed; the 1 failure was already there before the patch |
| OpenInference: root span OK on a failed run | 4 runs, passed on try 3 of the last | 5 scenarios OK → ERROR | 298 passed |
| neatlogs: failed `messages.stream()` shows OK | 2 runs, passed on try 1 | OK, no exception event → ERROR with one | 530 passed, same 1 error as before (a module that needs `google.genai`) |

Patching left no new mismatch in the full scenario library. Leads dropped 32 → 27 for OpenLLMetry, 19 → 14 for OpenInference and 35 → 31 for neatlogs.

**Model cost:** the key's spend went from $0.25 to $5.99 ($5.73) over 11 fix runs. The per-run figures add up to $5.42; the proxy's spend figure lags, as it did for the planner.

**Things that went wrong, all recorded in `hackathon.md`:**
- I found three holes in my own verifier during the runs. The clone wasn't reset between tries, new tests were left out of the suite comparison, and a suite that didn't run at all counted as "same failures". Because of them I withdrew two passes (one OpenLLMetry, one neatlogs) and reran those findings under the fixed rules.
- A note I wrote for the model said the Agents SDK always puts the error on the agent span. The recorded spans show it doesn't, and that cost OpenInference tries until I corrected it.
- Some new test functions also pass without the patch (3 of 4 for OpenLLMetry). Most are guards that a successful run stays OK, but the two OpenLLMetry wrapper tests would pass either way. The verifier now names such tests in every log, and each fix rests on the tests that do fail before, plus the scenarios and the repro.
- Known limits of the patches: OpenInference marks the run ERROR on any non-tool span error, even one the SDK later recovers from. neatlogs records no partial text or tokens when a stream fails.
- OpenLLMetry's own Agents SDK test suite tries to upload traces with its fake key and gets a 401. No real key is in that environment, and no key value appears in any written file.

The claude.ai Paybox and arvix MCP servers need authorising in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. Nothing in this task needed them.
